articles.title: Work, classes suspended in NCR, 16 provinces starting 1 p.m. on Aug. 28
articles.summary: Work in government offices and classes at all levels in public and private schools in the National Capital Region (NCR) and 16 provinces was suspended starting 1 p.m. Friday, Aug. 28, due to the…

blocks.text: Work in government offices and classes at all levels in public and private schools in the National Capital Region (NCR) and 16 provinces was suspended starting 1 p.m. Friday, Aug. 28, due to the expected further enhancement of the Southwest Monsoon by a low-pressure area that has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
The suspension was ordered under Memorandum Circular No. 132 issued by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC).

The areas covered are NCR, Abra, Benguet, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Bataan, Bulacan, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Tarlac, Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, Rizal, Oriental Mindoro, and Occidental Mindoro.
Government agencies involved in the delivery of basic and health services, disaster preparedness and response, and other vital services will continue their operations despite the suspension.
The circular said these agencies must continue rendering the necessary services during the period covered by the suspension.
Local chief executives may also implement localized cancellation or suspension of classes and/or work in government offices in other areas, pursuant to relevant laws, rules, and regulations.
The suspension of work or adoption of alternative work arrangements in the private sector will be left to management's discretion.
The suspension comes as authorities anticipate further strengthening of the Southwest Monsoon due to the low-pressure area that has entered the Philippine Area of Responsibility.

articles.title: Nepal flash flood 'unlikely' in PH --weather specialist
articles.summary: A weather specialist of weather bureau PAGASA on Friday said he believed that the landslide and flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 1:00pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
A weather specialist from PAGASA believes that the flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

“Based on ‘yung ating construction ng mga kailugan po sa ngayon is somehow hindi naman ganoon ka-drastic talaga, hindi comparable doon sa nangyari sa may area ng Himalayas kasi sobrang lawak naman po atsaka ang tataas talaga ng mga bundok nila doon,” PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Friday.

(Based on the current construction of our rivers, it is somehow not that drastic and is not comparable to what happened in the Himalayan region, which is much more extensive and has much higher mountains.)

“‘Yung potential energy coming from ‘yung pinakamataas papunta sa ibaba, talagang sobra ‘yung impact. Unlike dito na, yes may tendency na talagang dumami ‘yung tubig, pero ‘yung ragasa po hindi naman siya nakikita halos maladelubyo,” he added.
Other Stories

(The potential energy from the highest point moving down to the lower areas has a tremendous impact. Unlike here, where there is a tendency for the volume of water to increase, but we are not really seeing a massive surge that would cause a catastrophe.)
The flash floods and landslides killed at least 165 people and swept away entire villages.
Rivers, dams
When asked about possible landslides from mountains falling into dams, Estareja said that the country has no glaciers.
He also assured that the the government has a warning system in place.

“Kung magkaroon man ng ganoong instance na sobrang lakas ng ulan sa taas and then nagkaroon ng pagkasira ng gates and then nag burst open ‘yung ating mga rivers. At least po meron tayong mga warnings,” he said.

(If such an instance were to occur where there is extremely heavy rainfall in the upper areas, followed by damage to the gates and the rivers suddenly bursting open, at least we have warnings in place.)

According to Maki Pulido’s report on Saksi, though experts are still looking into the cause of the incident, University of the Philippines (UP) Resillience Institute Executive Director Mahar Lagmay said what occured may be a “debris flow.”
“Parang baha pero may laman na mga bato, graba, buhangin na pagka umagos ay parang wet concrete. Debris flow ang tawag diyan. Boulders na tangay-tangay nung baha na more than 50% ang bato,” he said.

(It is like a flood, but it carries rocks, gravel, and sand, and when it flows, it behaves like wet concrete. That is called a debris flow. Boulders are carried along by the flood, with more than 50% of the flow consisting of rocks.)
Lagmay said a debris flow occurred at Compostela Valley in 2012, where more than 500 people died, while several barangays in Oriental Mindoro were burried in 2015 by rocks from a debris flow.
“Marami tayong bundok. Kapag nagkaroon ng landslide because of a storm, thousands of landslides doon sa mountains, meron tayong source material,” he said.
(We have many mountains. When a storm causes landslides, potentially resulting in thousands of landslides in the mountains, we have a source of material.)
He said that the UP Resillience Institute has identified more than 1,000 places that has communities along the river. —Joahna Casilao/ VAL, GMA News

articles.title: DILG: Over 200 BFP personnel under probe over 'slot-for-sale' recruitment scheme
articles.summary: More than 200 personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) are being investigated over an alleged “slot-for-sale” recruitment scheme, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)…
articles.byline: JON VIKTOR D. CABUENAS, GMA News

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 12:56pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

More than 200 personnel of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) are being investigated over an alleged “slot-for-sale” recruitment scheme, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) said Friday.
At a press conference, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the investigation covers personnel nationwide and is part of a broader effort to eliminate corruption within the BFP.
“Binabalaan ko na ang lahat ng opisyal ng BFP. Lumabas na kayo ngayon at umamin kayo o hahabulin namin kayo hanggang matapos ang career niyo,” Remulla said.
“Ang iniimbestigahan namin ngayon ay lumagpas ng 200 tao na tungkol sa slots for sale,” he added.
Other Stories

(We are warning all (involved) BFP officials. You better come out and admit your fault or we will go after you until your career ends. We are investigating over 200 people over the slots for sale [scheme].)
The investigation followed an entrapment operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) Region 3 in San Fernando City, Pampanga on August 24.
The operation resulted in the arrest of a 32-year-old BFP personnel who was caught accepting P300,000 from the complainant in exchange for securing a position in the bureau.
Other applicants allegedly paid between P100,000 and P800,000 for BFP slots under the illegal scheme.
“It's a P15 billion a year industry,” Remulla said.
A senior BFP officer in Calabarzon allegedly linked to the recruitment scheme was also relieved from their post and placed under restrictive duty pending investigation.
Remulla vowed to clean the BFP and resolve the matter within six months. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: PH batters bow to Venezuela, miss World Cup final berth
articles.summary: The Philippines missed a chance to qualify in the finals of next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup after falling short against Venezuela, 0-10, in the final match of its group stage in Tainan, Taiwan…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: A few hours after absorbing a painful 2-8 defeat at the hands of host Chinese Taipei, the Nationals continued their struggle against the more experienced Venezuelans to finish the group stage with a 2-3 win-loss record.

blocks.text: (Photo from PABA)

The Philippines missed a chance to qualify in the finals of next year’s Women’s Baseball World Cup after falling short against Venezuela, 0-10, in the final match of its group stage in Tainan, Taiwan on Thursday, Aug. 29.

A few hours after absorbing a painful 2-8 defeat at the hands of host Chinese Taipei, the Nationals continued their struggle against the more experienced Venezuelans to finish the group stage with a 2-3 win-loss record.
They finished fourth behind unbeaten Japan (5-0), Venezuela (4-1) and Chinese Taipei (3-2), who claimed the top 3 slots allocated for next year’s finals in Rockford, Illinois.
The three qualified teams joined the United States, Australia and Canada, who clinched spots by finishing in the top 3 of their group stage held in Rockford last July.
Despite falling short of their goal, the Nationals still showed promise with victories over world No. 7 Cuba, 6-0, and Great Britain, 6-2, last Wednesday, Aug. 26.
They also lost to Japan, 0-3, and Cuba, 0-6.

articles.title: Trump administration seeks to restrict internships for international students
articles.summary: The August 24 memo resulted in some schools, including the University of California, Los Angeles and the University of California, Berkeley, pausing certain applications for work authorizations for…

items: The Trump administration issued a memo restricting internship work authorizations for international students, warning universities of potential loss of certification for non-compliance.
Some universities, including UCLA and UC Berkeley, have paused certain work authorization applications while reviewing the new federal guidance, which is seen as more restrictive.

The administration has also targeted universities over various issues, including diversity initiatives and protests, leading to allegations of bias in admissions practices and revocation of visas for student protesters.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA — President Donald Trump‘s administration has issued a memo for universities that seeks to restrict issuance of certain internship work authorizations for international students as the federal government warned that colleges not complying with the regulations may lose certification to enroll foreign students.

The federal memo dated August 24 said the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, which is part of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, has “observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorizations that appear to violate regulatory requirements which permit CPT only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum.”
“Failure to comply with SEVP regulations may result in an institution losing certification to enroll foreign students,” the memo said.

It resulted in some schools, including the University of California, Los Angeles and the University of California, Berkeley, pausing certain applications for work authorizations for international students.
“UCLA has paused certain Curricular Practical Training authorizations while it reviews recent federal guidance and determines next steps,” a UCLA spokesperson said.

UC Berkeley’s international office said the August 24 memo was “more narrow in focus, more direct, and includes content that is more restrictive in nature.” The federal government had also issued an earlier memo in mid-August.
UC Berkeley’s international office said it is unlikely that it will process certain work authorization applications “in the near future” and urged those international students to plan accordingly.

It said it will continue processing “degree-requirement” CPT as normal and would resume processing “Doctoral Dissertation and Master’s Thesis Research CPT.” The office said it would consult legal experts to develop new processes aligning with new federal requirements.

“Nothing about these regulations has changed,” the Department of Homeland Security, ICE’s parent, said in a statement. “However, schools and employers should consider themselves on notice: under President Trump, abuse of this generous system will no longer be tolerated.”

Trump has targeted universities with probes and funding threats over issues like pro-Palestinian protests against US ally Israel’s assault on Gaza, diversity initiatives, climate programs, and transgender policies. Rights advocates have raised free speech, academic freedom, and due process concerns.

Separately, the US Justice Department alleged on Thursday admissions practices at the George Washington University School of Medicine and Health Services favored Black and Hispanic applicants, citing findings of a probe as the Trump administration continued its diversity crackdown.
“We are disappointed by the DOJ’s conclusions, which we believe are incorrect,” the university said, saying the admissions policies were in compliance with law and not discriminatory.
The Justice Department has alleged similar bias at other schools, saying the department aims for settlement talks. If those efforts fail, the department will file suit, it said.
Trump’s administration has also revoked visas of student protesters over pro-Palestinian protests that it casts as antisemitic and sympathetic to extremists.

Protesters, including some Jewish groups, say opposition to Israel’s assault on Gaza and its occupation of Palestinian territories is not antisemitic and advocacy for Palestinian rights is not the same as supporting extremism. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation donates 1,000 sacks of rice to Baguio, Benguet LGUs
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY – The Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation distributed 1,000 sacks of 5 kilos of rice to three local government units for residents affected by the previous typhoon and the southwest…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY – The Filipino at Tsino Magkaibigan Foundation distributed 1,000 sacks of 5 kilos of rice to three local government units for residents affected by the previous typhoon and the southwest monsoon.

The donation, spearheaded by the Federation of Filipino Chinese Chambers of Commerce & Industry, Inc.-Baguio Chapter led by Peter Ng, together with its members, delivered 300 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) to the Benguet provincial government, on August 27, which were received by Governor Melchor Diclas.
Diclas expressed his deep gratitude to the Baguio Filipino-Chinese community for its continuing support, particularly during times of calamity.
In the capital town of La Trinidad, officials also received 200 sacks (5 kilos each) of rice provided by the group for the disaster victims.

Another 500 sacks of rice (5 kilos each) were personally delivered by Ng and his group to the Office of the City Social Welfare and Development Office in Baguio City, which were received by City Administrator Vittorio Jericho Cawis and OCWD Officer Liza Balungayan.

“On behalf of Mayor Benjamin Magalong, thank you very much for the tireless support to the city government of the Filipino-Chinese community, not only during the disaster, but also for their continued support for the city’s tourism development programs,” said Cawis.
He said that based on ODSWDO data, more than 1,000 families were severely affected by the southwest monsoon.
It can be recalled that last year, the foundation also donated 1,000 bags of five kilos of rice to these LGUs to be distributed to those affected by the typhoon.

“In our groups, and with the support of the foundation, this is our traditional work to deliver aid to disaster victims. On these occasions, we want to show that we are Filipinos who will continue to help the community,” said Ng.

articles.title: Japanese Ambassador Endo bids farewell, thanks Filipinos for support and friendship
articles.summary: Outgoing Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya bade farewell to Filipinos on Friday, Aug. 28, as he ended his two-and-a-half-year tour of duty, describing his time in the country as…

blocks.text: Outgoing Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines Endo Kazuya bade farewell to Filipinos on Friday, Aug. 28, as he ended his two-and-a-half-year tour of duty, describing his time in the country as "truly unforgettable."
In an X post, Endo thanked Filipinos for their "unwavering" support and friendship, saying he was deeply humbled to have served as ambassador "at the height of our two countries’ partnership."
"Taos-pusong pasasalamat, Pilipinas (My sincerest thanks, Philippines)!” he wrote.
“These two and a half years have been truly unforgettable, and I am deeply humbled to have served as Japanese Ambassador to the Philippines at the height of our two countries’ partnership," he added.
In a video accompanying the post, Endo also thanked Filipinos for their friendship and support.
"Maraming salamat sa walang humpay ninyong suporta at pagkakaibigan (Thank you very much for your unwavering support and friendship),” he said.
“Hanggang sa muli! Mata ne (Until we meet again. See you)!” he added.

Endo’s farewell message came a day after President Marcos honored him during a farewell call at Malacañang, where the President conferred on him the Order of Sikatuna, Grand Cross with Distinction, for his contributions to strengthening Philippine-Japan relations.

According to the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), Endo was recognized for promoting bilateral exchanges and deepening cooperation in defense, security, and development cooperation, as well as supporting Philippine priorities in infrastructure, education, transportation, maritime domain awareness, and human resource development.

The PCO also cited Endo's efforts to advance Japan's longstanding commitment to peace and development in Mindanao, including support for the peace process, grassroots development, and the transition of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

The award likewise recognized his efforts to mobilize Japanese humanitarian and development assistance during natural disasters and recent regional crises, as well as initiatives that fostered friendship, mutual understanding, and goodwill between Filipinos and Japanese.
The Order of Sikatuna is conferred on individuals who have rendered exceptional and meritorious service to the Philippines or made outstanding contributions to Philippine-Japan relations.

The Philippines and Japan are marking 70 years of normalized relations this year, with 15 years of Strengthened Strategic Partnership since 2011, and bilateral ties having expanded across economic, development, security, and people-to-people cooperation.

articles.title: Danielle Smith takes questions at virtual town hall on data centres in Alberta, NDP calls for pause
articles.summary: Premier Danielle Smith and three of her ministers spent an hour Thursday fielding calls and online questions from Albertans who say they are concerned about artificial intelligence data centres being…

image.caption: Premier Danielle Smith said her government is considering feedback from Albertans who attended town halls to express concerns around data centres. Smith is seen in this photo speaking to media in Calgary on Feb. 1, 2024. (Emilio Avalos/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Premier Danielle Smith and three of her ministers spent an hour Thursday fielding calls and online questions from Albertans who say they are concerned about artificial intelligence data centres being built in the province.

The virtual town hall was tame compared to the two in-person events held earlier this month, where Technology Minister Nate Glubish was repeatedly hit with criticism, profanity and demands for additional safeguards.
For Thursday's call, Albertans could either submit questions online or, if they registered in advance, over the phone.
Moderator Justin Wright, the province's primary care minister, said over 12,500 people had tuned in.
Smith's government has been trying to position Alberta as an ideal destination for data centres, saying they could generate new jobs and billions in royalties and taxes for the province.
The premier has said the town halls are about finding "blind spots" in the government's regulatory framework.
Alberta Ministers face barrage of opposition to data centres

But, as with the previous events, nobody who spoke Thursday expressed any excitement about having the major computing complexes built in the province in the first place. One caller did say he was excited to be on the call with "the premier and her entourage," but he didn't ask a question or mention data centres.

The event started with Smith addressing many of the concerns the government has already heard, including about water use, location selection and setbacks, and potential electricity bill hikes — all issues that callers would bring up.

Water usage was a popular topic, with many callers questioning Smith and her ministers for saying that projects to date — namely the $13-billion campus north of Edmonton being proposed by tech giant Meta — will have limited water use.
The facility is to have a closed-loop cooling system, and both the company and the government have said its annual water use would be equivalent to a golf course.

One caller, identified as David from Calgary, asked why the province wasn't also accounting for the water that will be used by the adjacent $4.6-billion natural gas power plant, built solely to power Meta's facility.
"They'll be using loads of water. I mean, enormous amounts," he said.

items: Alberta minister faces more fury at second town hall on AI data centres

blocks.text: Smith said his point was well taken, but also said other heavy industries use massive amounts of water. She specifically mentioned a pulp mill in northern Alberta that she recently toured, saying it used seven billion litres of water per year.
"We don't say that you're not allowed to use water at all," she said.
Another caller, Peggy, asked why the government was willing to risk bringing in more heavy water users when parts of the province have seen water restrictions in recent years.
"It doesn't seem like a really smart, long-term idea," she said.
The issue of jobs also came up when one caller asked whether Albertans would be prioritized.

Smith said that was the goal, adding it was also why the referendum her government has scheduled for Oct. 19 will feature questions about whether Alberta should take more control over immigration and temporary foreign worker rules.
"That's certainly what I think should be done, and I want to just make sure that Albertans agree with us on that," the premier said.
Thursday's event also saw the government poll callers and those online about whether they supported setbacks to protect communities from having data centres built too close to homes.

items: Alberta Utilities Commission rejects power plant for Olds data centre plan

blocks.text: Proximity to homes is why a provincial regulator rejected a major data centre project last week in the town of Olds, north of Calgary. Smith had said on Wednesday that her government was already considering developing guidance for setbacks.
Wright shared that 57 per cent of respondents "strongly supported" the measure.

He also conducted another poll at the end of the event, asking those on the call to identify their greatest concern about data centres, with options including electricity affordability, grid reliability, water use, or other. The results weren't shared before the call ended.
Thursday's town hall began just hours after the Opposition called for a moratorium on AI data centres until stricter rules are put in place.
NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi told reporters that Smith's government has rushed ahead and rubber-stamped projects without clear guidelines or by first hearing Albertans' concerns.
Projects should go through impact assessments to ensure significant community benefits, permanent jobs, and that life-cycle plans for when facilities run their course are in place, he said.

items: Man planning protests against data centres as Alberta government announces town hall events

blocks.text: They're the concerns he said his party heard most when it hosted its own data centre town halls over the summer.
"The UCP failed to create a process that Albertans can have confidence in," Nenshi said.
He said his party's proposal would provide certainty for residents and those behind the projects.
The rejection of the Olds proposal, which had been turned down once before for other reasons, represents a government failure for not having clear expectations for developers, Nenshi added.
"There is no framework in place, and they're making it up as they go along," he said.
"Would a company like that want to invest in Alberta again after they were treated this way by the government?"

items: Why are there suddenly so many data centres planned in Canada? Your questions answered

blocks.text: The province didn't immediately respond to questions about the NDP's call for a moratorium on Thursday.
The issue of reclamation did come up during the town hall when a caller asked who would be stuck with the infrastructure should a data centre be abandoned.
Glubish said it would fall to the province. He said he was confident another company would come in and take the warehouse for "pennies on the dollar."
He also said an abandoned power plant would be considered a new asset for the province, and that the government would look to keep it running so that power is still fed to the electricity grid.
Smith added that reclamation for data centres was different than wind turbines, which her government requires operators to have clean-up plans for before being built.
"We have a high level of confidence that those [data centre] buildings will be able to be used for something else," she said.
The government's fourth and final data centre town hall is scheduled for Sept. 11 in Grande Prairie, though the premier isn't scheduled to attend.

articles.title: WHAT WE KNOW SO FAR: 1 Filipino still missing after deadly Nepal flash flood
articles.summary: One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 12:34pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community to locate the missing national.
Philippine Embassy in India Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo said Friday that they have yet to receive information on the Filipino whose disappearance was reported following the disaster.
“Until now, we are still waiting for information about the missing Filipino which was reported yesterday,” Pelayo said in a Super Radyo dzBB interview.
The Filipino is among the 667 foreign nationals from 32 countries listed as still missing in the update released by Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday evening.
Other Stories
Nepalese authorities said 359 bodies had been recovered at that point.
Filipino community in Nepal accounted for
Pelayo said the Philippine Embassy has maintained close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal and that those they have accounted for are safe.
“Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for,” she said.

Most members of the Filipino community are in Kathmandu, according to Pelayo. She said around 90% of the profiles they have are spouses of Nepalese nationals, while the percentage of Filipino professionals in the country is “very minimal.”

The Philippine government earlier said there were 18 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Nepal based on Overseas Workers Welfare Administration records, while Department of Foreign Affairs data showed 128 Filipinos in the country.
Rescue efforts continue
Pelayo said Nepalese authorities continue rescue operations in areas affected by the flash flood, although access to some locations remains difficult.
The Philippine official also noted that getting information from the affected areas has been difficult, saying it would be challenging for her to personally reach the location.

Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an emergency response team to coordinate search and rescue operations, verify information concerning missing foreign nationals and provide consular assistance. It has also urged families and diplomatic missions to rely on official channels and avoid circulating unverified information.
The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a torrent of water, rock, ice and mud through Himalayan river systems along the Nepal-China border.
A Reuters report on Thursday quoting the Nepali police said that 359 had died, with dozens of bodies swept down into the plains from where they were being recovered.

Rescuers searched for survivors in the debris-strewn valleys and hillsides of Nepal on Thursday while more than 1,000 people remained missing there and in neighboring China after a wall of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a mountain river, triggering a catastrophic flash flood.
The Philippine government has also expressed condolences to Nepal and those affected by the disaster.

articles.title: Philippine exports, imports lose steam as second half begins
articles.summary: Philippine merchandise trade lost momentum at the start of the second half of 2026, as both exports and imports posted slower annual growth in July and fell in value from the previous month. The…

blocks.text: Philippine merchandise trade lost momentum at the start of the second half of 2026, as both exports and imports posted slower annual growth in July and fell in value from the previous month.

The latest preliminary Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data released on Friday, Aug. 28, showed exports grew by 10.8 percent year-on-year to $8.15 billion in July, sharply slower than the 25-percent expansion in June. Imports likewise rose by 19.8 percent to $14.12 billion, easing from the 25-percent growth recorded a month ago.

In value terms, exports fell by $681.31 million, or 7.7 percent, from the revised monthly record high of $8.83 billion in June, while imports declined by $204.52 million, or 1.4 percent, from $14.33 billion. As a result, total external trade dropped by $885.83 million, or 3.8 percent, month-on-month to $22.27 billion from $23.16 billion.
The July export value was the lowest since May, when outbound shipments amounted to $7.95 billion, while imports were also at their lowest since May’s $14.05 billion.
The slower trade performance came despite continued strong demand for Philippine electronic products, which remained the country’s top export commodity.

Electronics exports reached $4.79 billion in July, accounting for 58.8 percent of total outbound shipments. They also recorded the biggest annual increase among commodity groups, rising by $869.72 million from $3.92 billion a year ago.

Other commodities that contributed to the annual increase in exports were gold, which rose by $79.34 million; electronic equipment and parts, up by $71.81 million; machinery and transport equipment, up by $50.06 million; and woodcrafts and furniture, up by $30.92 million.

By major type of goods, manufactured goods remained the largest source of export earnings at $6.61 billion, equivalent to 81.1 percent of total. Mineral products followed at $776.61 million, or 9.5 percent of total, while agro-based products accounted for $548.95 million, or 6.7 percent.

Despite the July slowdown, exports in the first seven months of the year climbed by 12.9 percent to $54.92 billion from $48.67 billion in the same period last year, the highest January-to-July export value since the series began in 1991.

The United States (US) remained the Philippines’ biggest export market in July, accounting for $1.68 billion, or 20.7 percent of total exports. It was followed by Hong Kong at $1.29 billion, China at $919.82 million, Japan at $856.6 million, and Singapore at $401.17 million.
On the import side, electronic products also posted the biggest annual increase, surging by $1.75 billion to $4.6 billion and accounting for 32.6 percent of total imports.

This was followed by mineral fuels, lubricants and related materials, which increased by $502.71 million to $1.95 billion, and cereals and cereal preparations, which rose by $187.36 million to $561.06 million.

Raw materials and intermediate goods comprised the biggest share of imports at $5.71 billion, or 40.4 percent, followed by capital goods at $3.84 billion, or 27.2 percent, and consumer goods at $2.58 billion, or 18.3 percent.
From January to July, imports increased by 18.9 percent to $92.26 billion from $77.58 billion a year ago, also the highest first-seven-month import value since the series began in 1991.

China remained the country’s largest source of imported goods, supplying $4.17 billion, or 29.5 percent of total imports in July. It was followed by South Korea with $1.8 billion, Japan with $1.11 billion, Indonesia with $807.75 million, and the US with $766.61 million.

With imports continuing to outpace exports, the country’s balance of trade in goods posted a deficit of $5.97 billion in July, 34.9 percent wider than the $4.43-billion shortfall a year ago and the widest since the $6.1-billion deficit recorded in May.

Total external trade nevertheless remained 16.3 percent higher than the $19.14 billion recorded in July last year, although its annual growth also slowed from 25 percent in June. Imports accounted for 63.4 percent of July trade, while exports comprised the remaining 36.6 percent. - with a report from Danielle T. Bayani

articles.title: Red rainfall warning up over Zambales, Bataan; NCR under yellow alert
articles.summary: Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.

blocks.text: Motorists and pedestrians are drenched during a heavy downpour in Quezon City as the habagat continues to batter in Metro Manila and neighboring provinces with strong winds and heavy rainfall on Aug. 8, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel de Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — Zambales and parts of Bataan were placed under a red rainfall warning on Friday morning, August 28, as the southwest monsoon or habagat continues to dump heavy rains over parts of Luzon.
In its heavy rainfall advisory issued at 11 a.m., state weather bureau PAGASA said that serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas under the red warning level.
The following areas are under the red warning level:

items: Zambales
Bataan: Morong, Hermosa and Dinalupihan

blocks.text: PAGASA said flooding is still threatening in areas under the orange warning level, which covers:

items: Pampanga
Tarlac
Bulacan
Bataan: Abucay, Bagac, Balanga, Limay, Mariveles, Orani, Orion, Pilar and Samal

Nueva Ecija: Guimba, Santo Domingo, Talavera, Llanera, Rizal, Bongabon, Gabaldon, Laur, Palayan, General Mamerto Natividad, Cabanatuan, Aliaga, Quezon, Licab, Zaragoza, Jaen, Santa Rosa, San Leonardo, San Isidro, San Antonio, Cabiao, Gapan, General Tinio and Peñaranda

blocks.text: Meanwhile, flooding is possible in flood-prone areas under the yellow warning level, including:

items: Metro Manila
Rizal
Cavite: Bacoor, Imus, Kawit, Noveleta, Cavite City, Rosario, Tanza, Naic, Ternate, Maragondon, General Trias, Magallanes, General Emilio Aguinaldo and Alfonso
Batangas: Nasugbu, Lian and Calatagan
Nueva Ecija: Carranglan, Cuyapo, Lupao, Nampicuan, Pantabangan, San Jose, Muñoz and Talugtug

blocks.text: PAGASA said light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains are also expected over Laguna and parts of Batangas and Cavite within the next three hours.

In Batangas, these include Batangas City, Ibaan, San Jose, Agoncillo, Alitagtag, Balayan, Balete, Bauan, Calaca, Tanauan, Cuenca, Laurel, Lemery, Lipa, Mabini, Malvar, Mataasnakahoy, San Luis, San Nicolas, San Pascual, Santa Teresita, Santo Tomas, Taal, Talisay, Tingloy and Tuy.
In Cavite, the affected areas are Amadeo, Indang, Mendez, Silang, Tagaytay, Trece Martires, Carmona, Dasmarinas and General Mariano Alvarez.
Light to moderate rains with occasional heavy rains are also affecting General Nakar, Quezon. The conditions may persist within three hours and could affect nearby areas.
Meanwhile, PAGASA said that it was monitoring a low pressure area inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility as of 8 a.m.
The weather disturbance has a medium chance of developing into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.

articles.title: It works! Lucena inventor creates trash-collecting robot from recycled materials
articles.summary: LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city. The device…

blocks.text: (Photo by Isagani Inciong via Danny Estacio)
LUCENA CITY, Quezon - An innovative method for cleaning waterways was demonstrated at the Iyam River using an improvised garbage-collecting robot made from recycled materials in this city.
The device was constructed using old plastic containers, aluminum, and galvanized wire mesh.
It is equipped with a garbage lifter designed to easily gather and collect floating debris.
The robot is operated via a remote control—similar to those used in computer games—that controls a small motor attached to the unit.
According to Isagani Inciong, an electronics technician and the device's inventor, he conceived the project to help reduce floating river debris, particularly plastic waste.
Tests conducted at the Iyam River proved the robot effective at gathering and retrieving floating trash.
Inciong added that aside from being fun to operate, the robot offers significant environmental benefits.
He believes that if more people use or "play" with this type of robot, a larger volume of waste can be recovered from waterways.

He also called on local government units (LGUs) to take notice of his invention and expressed willingness to collaborate with authorities to refine the design and build a larger version of the robot to support more extensive river rehabilitation efforts.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Misamis Oriental family deaths in 2021 due to COVID-19, not vaccines
articles.summary: A viral Facebook reel recycles a report from a 2021 incident involving four family members in Misamis Oriental; the health department has clarified that the deaths were associated with COVID-19…

blocks.text: Claim: Four members of one family in Laguindingan, Misamis Oriental, died because of COVID-19 vaccines after receiving their jabs.

Why we fact-checked this: A widely shared Facebook reel claims that four members of the same family died because of COVID-19 vaccines. Posted on August 16, 2026, it garnered around 19,400 reactions, 1,700 comments, and 19,000 shares as of writing.
The reel was posted by the Facebook account Unsa Gyod Gisulti SaBibliya, which has around 60,000 followers.
The account’s biography shows an anti-vaccination position, stating: “Va666ines= Mark Of The Beast! ✓Mandated (Rev13:16) ✓Required (Rev13:17) ✓Deceit (Rev18:23,19:20).”
It also has multiple reels opposing vaccines, many of which use the phrase, “Va666$in TATAK666 ng Antikristo nililinlang at nilalason mga kabataan.”
(Vaccines are marks of the Antichrist, deceiving and poisoning the youth.)

The post presents the incident, using a news report from GMA Regional TV, as evidence that COVID-19 vaccines were responsible for the deaths and questions the Department of Health (DOH)’s explanation of the case.
The facts: The four deaths were real, occurring between August 1 and 8, 2021, but available evidence does not support the claim that COVID-19 vaccination caused them.
According to an August 21, 2021 report by the Philippine News Agency, the DOH Region 10 found that the four individuals showed COVID-19 symptoms.
About 10 family members and neighbors were also infected. Investigators identified possible exposure at a wake in Barangay Patag, Cagayan de Oro City, and at a family birthday gathering.
Jasper Kent Ola, the nurse-epidemiologist who supervised the investigation, explained that the deaths occurred successively because of the different infection and incubation periods of the virus.
The Philippine Information Agency (PIA) later reported on August 23, 2021 that the four deceased family members tested positive for COVID-19 through RT-PCR tests.

The DOH-10 Regional Adverse Effect Following Immunization Committee also conducted a causality assessment based on case-tracking reports and found that the cases were “inconsistent with causal association to immunization.”
Investigators concluded that the individuals were likely already incubating the virus around the time of immunization.

Vaccination in the Philippines: The Facebook reel surfaced amid the DOH’s rollout of its nationwide Measles-Rubella Supplementary Immunization Activity this month. In an August 27 PIA report, the DOH said false information about vaccines continues to circulate on social media and may discourage parents from having their children immunized.
To counter this, the health department is partnering with local government units to conduct health education sessions and share reliable information on vaccines through social media.
Earlier, Rappler debunked circulating posts casting doubt on the safety of the measles-rubella vaccines. – Ahyenne Neleah Estacio/Rappler.com

Ahyenne Neleah Estacio is a graduating Bachelor of Arts in Communication student and campus journalist at Holy Angel University. The current senior editor and former editor-in-chief of The Angelite, she is an Aries Rufo Fellow for 2026.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: No place for violence, bullying in Baguio - Mayor Magalong
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City. This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY -- There is no place for violence, bullying, or any form of abuse, especially against children and young people in Baguio City.
This was emphasized by Mayor Benjamin Magalong as he assured that the two separate violent incidents involving high school students are now being handled by the Baguio City Police Office.
Magalong urged the public not to circulate a video involving one of the cases to prevent online abuse.
"While we do not condone these acts among the youth, we should also respect the dignity, privacy, and well-being of the children involved."

He asked the public not to "share, repost, or further circulate the video" as further dissemination could expose minors to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse.
Magalong urged the public to allow police authorities, school officials, and social workers to address the two separate cases judiciously.
“Let us not amplify violence. Let us protect our children and help build a safer, kinder, and more respectful Baguio,” he said.
The police said the two cases are being handled separately with details treated confidentially because minors are involved.
The first incident involving students reportedly occurred outside the school premises of a high school at around 3 p.m. on August 26.
Investigation report said complaints were filed with Police Station 2 and the minors involved, described as Grade 9 and Grade 10 students, have been identified.
Personnel of the Women and Children Protection Desk (WCPD) coordinated with the school authorities while appropriate intervention was undertaken with the assistance of social workers.
Police Station 2 had scheduled another coordination meeting on August 28 to discuss the matter and the appropriate interventions.
The second incident reportedly involved Grade 7 and Grade 9 students from another secondary school and was reported to Police Station 5 at around 1 p.m. on August 27.
The incident allegedly happened during recess on August 24 inside a classroom causing an injury to the complainant.

Police said WCPD personnel coordinated with the school principal and class advisers and a dialogue was later held with the students and their parents or guardians with administrative sanctions expected to be imposed.

articles.title: DSWD, DDB pilot program to curb drug abuse risks among street children, out-of-school youth
articles.summary: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and…

blocks.text: Children in street situations and out-of-school youth will be among the first beneficiaries of a new intervention that combines drug abuse prevention education with family, community, and psychosocial support.

The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), in partnership with the Dangerous Drugs Board (DDB), is piloting “Program Silong,” an integrated program to be implemented through Special Drug Education Centers (SDECs).
The agencies conducted a week-long training for the program’s pilot implementation from Aug. 24 to 28 in Quezon City.
DSWD Special Assistant to the Secretary for Innovations Helen Suzara said the initiative seeks to strengthen drug and substance abuse prevention efforts among children and young people.
“Silong is an important step in strengthening our collective efforts towards drug abuse prevention, particularly among children and the young people,” Suzara said during the opening of the training.
The program has four components covering drug abuse prevention education, family involvement and support, community mobilization, and psychosocial and auxiliary services.
The education component includes toolkits designed for children, early to late adolescents, and parents or caregivers.

The family component will provide interventions to help parents and caregivers support drug abuse prevention efforts, while the community component will encourage communities to develop and implement prevention activities.
The psychosocial component will use pre- and post-assessments to identify the needs of children in street situations and out-of-school youth and monitor their progress.
Suzara described Program Silong as “a pioneering initiative, the first of its kind in the Philippines and in the ASEAN region.”
The program will initially be piloted in Muntinlupa City, Occidental Mindoro, and Zamboanga del Sur.

DSWD said the initiative is in line with its mandate under the implementing rules and regulations of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, to provide drug abuse prevention and developmental services to vulnerable children and youth.
It will also involve community volunteers and local government implementers in carrying out prevention activities in the pilot areas.

articles.title: College student killed, girlfriend wounded in Ilocos Norte shooting
articles.summary: NUEVA ERA, Ilocos Norte — A 24-year-old college student was killed while his girlfriend was wounded when they were shot by a motorcycle-riding gunman in front of their residence in Barangay Uguis…

blocks.text: NUEVA ERA, Ilocos Norte — A 24-year-old college student was killed while his girlfriend was wounded when they were shot by a motorcycle-riding gunman in front of their residence in Barangay Uguis here Thursday night, August 27.
Police identified the fatality as alias "Jay,” a resident of Sitio Tres, Barangay Uguis.
His girlfriend, also a college student, and a resident of Burgos, Ilocos Norte, suffered gunshot wounds in the leg and abdomen.

Police said the victims had just arrived home at around 7:30 p.m. when a 19-year-old suspect, a resident of the same barangay, allegedly approached them on a motorcycle and fired four shots from a still unknown firearm
Jay sustained multiple gunshot wounds. He and his girlfriend were rushed to a hospital in Sinait, Ilocos Sur, but he was declared dead upon arrival.
The suspect is now the subject of a hot-pursuit operation.
The Nueva Era police are continuing their investigation and awaiting the SOCO findings.

articles.title: School bag yields marijuana, 8 live bullets; student arrested in Tuguegarao
articles.summary: TUGUEGARAO CITY — A routine security check at a private school here led to the arrest of a 20-year-old college student after suspected marijuana and eight live 9mm rounds were allegedly found in his…

blocks.text: TUGUEGARAO CITY — A routine security check at a private school here led to the arrest of a 20-year-old college student after suspected marijuana and eight live 9mm rounds were allegedly found in his backpack on Monday, August 24.

Police said the student, identified only as alias “Mar,” a resident of Barangay Ngarag, Cabagan, Isabela, was stopped for inspection at about 11:56 a.m. at the school’s pedestrian entrance along Balzain Highway in Barangay Centro 12.
A female security officer conducting the routine bag inspection reportedly discovered two pieces of suspected marijuana weighing 1.78 grams and valued at about P213.
A glass tube reportedly containing marijuana residue and eight live 9mm ammunition were also found inside the backpack.
The discovery prompted the security officer to alert authorities, resulting in the student’s arrest and turnover to the Tuguegarao City Police Station.
Police said the confiscated items would be turned over to the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency Regional Office 2 for examination and proper disposition.
The student is facing charges under Sections 11 and 12 of Republic Act No. 9165, or the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, for alleged possession of marijuana and drug paraphernalia.
He is also facing a charge under Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Law on Firearms and Ammunition, for alleged illegal possession of the eight live rounds.
Authorities are continuing their investigation into the source and intended use of the ammunition and suspected illegal drugs.

articles.title: No more delayed PDL release: Remulla justifies proposed transfer of BJMP to DOJ
articles.summary: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) ought to be transferred to the Department of Justice (DOJ), if only to avoid delays in the release of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) due to messy…

blocks.text: The Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) ought to be transferred to the Department of Justice (DOJ), if only to avoid delays in the release of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) due to messy paperwork.
Thus, said DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla during the agency’s marathon budget hearing before the House Committee on Appropriations Thursday, Aug. 27.
It was Makabayan lawmaker ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio who raised the unfortunate issue of inmates being kept in BJMP custody because of the clerical matter.
Remulla responded by saying that it would be better to transfer the BJMP to the DOJ since the latter handles the records of PDLs.
“It is our position that the BJMP should be transferred under the [DOJ], under the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor),” he told Tinio, a deputy minority leader.
“Dalawang pong karpeta eh, may karpeta ang BJMP, may karpeta ang Bucor," noted the DILG chief (There are two folders, the BJMP has its own folder, and the BuCor has its own folder).
"I think it would be prudent for Congress to help us into combining the BuCor and BJMP into one facility since they perform the same jobs, basically, they just mirroring each other,” he reckoned.
Aside from the BJMP, Remulla also proposed transferring to the DOJ municipal and provincial jails.

“So we’re asking Congress for help, the President’s help, in combining the two agencies for more efficient use of resources and for fair treatment of the Persons Deprived of Liberty if they have to release of not,” Remulla said.

Under the present system, inmates or PDLs are detained in municipal, city, and provincial jails while their cases are being heard. Once sentenced, they are transferred to the New Bilibid Prison (NBP), which is managed by the Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) under the DOJ.
Located in Muntinlupa City, the NBP has a population of over 20,000, which is nearly 200 percent above its intended capacity.

articles.title: Trump administration illegally retaliated against Anthropic, judge rules
articles.summary: The AI startup has been at loggerheads with the Pentagon over the use of AI by the US military.

blocks.text: A judge has ruled the US Department of Defense acted unlawfully when it designated artificial intelligence (AI) startup Anthropic a supply chain risk, calling the move "illegal and baseless".

The company argued in the lawsuit that Defense Secretary Pete Hegeth overstepped his authority with the new designation. It followed Anthropic's refusal to allow the military to use its AI models for things that included surveillance or autonomous weapons.
US district judge Rita Lin said in the ruling that citing national security "is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics".
Anthropic welcomed the ruling. The BBC has contacted the Pentagon and the White House for comment.
Anthropic is focused on "working productively with the government to harness AI for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology," a spokesperson told the BBC.
Judge Lin said in the court filing that the Defense Department had acted unlawfully to order firms that do business with the US military to boycott Anthropic.
The Pentagon designated Anthropic as a supply-chain risk in February - a law typically reserved for companies based in countries that pose a threat to the US.
It marked the first time an American company had been publicly designated as such.
Anthropic's lawsuit said the government's actions were both "unprecedented and unlawful".
The Claude-maker said its models were not reliable enough to be safely used in weapons systems for the military. It added that it opposed its use for domestic surveillance as a violation of rights.
The Pentagon said at the time that private companies should not be able to constrain military action.

The White House had previously said Anthropic was "a radical left, woke company" attempting to control military activity" and argued the military was beholden to the US Constitution, "not any woke AI company's terms of service".
The Pentagon also argued that Anthropic's refusal to accept new contract terms raised concerns over what the company could do with its technology.
Anthropic said in its lawsuit that its business had been impacted by the government's actions and its right to freedom of speech had been violated.
Judge Lin said during an earlier round in the lawsuit that the government was trying to "cripple" the company and "chill public debate" over military use of AI.
"This appears to be classic First Amendment retaliation," the judge added.

articles.title: Parañaque cops seize loaded gun from construction worker
articles.summary: A construction worker was arrested after police found a loaded .38-caliber revolver during a search operation in Parañaque City on Thursday, Aug. 27. Police said the suspect, identified as Edwin, 39,…

blocks.text: The loaded .38-caliber revolver seized in Parañaque police operation (Photo from Parañaque City Police) ‎
A construction worker was arrested after police found a loaded .38-caliber revolver during a search operation in Parañaque City on Thursday, Aug. 27.
Police said the suspect, identified as Edwin, 39, of Hontiveros Compound, Barangay San Antonio, was arrested at around 5:10 p.m.
Members of the Parañaque City Police Station Intelligence Section served the search warrant issued by Judge Moises D. De Castro of the Parañaque Metropolitan Trial Court.
The operation resulted in the recovery of a .38-caliber revolver loaded with four live rounds of ammunition.
The suspect was detained at the police custodial facility and will face charges for violation of Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.

blocks.text: Another setback has hit KATSEYE, with the global girl group pulling out of Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival after Megan Skiendiel suffered an ankle injury during a tour rehearsal.
KATSEYE announced through Weverse that it would no longer perform at the women-led music festival, scheduled for Aug. 29 at Great Park in Irvine, California.
The group said Megan sprained her ankle during rehearsal and, after being evaluated by doctors, was advised to stay off it and allow it to properly heal ahead of KATSEYE’s upcoming tour.

“Megan sprained her ankle yesterday during tour rehearsal and after being evaluated by doctors, she has been advised to stay off it and allow it to properly heal so we can be ready for our upcoming tour,” the group said.
The members apologized to fans who had been looking forward to seeing them at the festival.
“We know how much our fans were looking forward to seeing us and it breaks our hearts to disappoint anyone who made plans to be there,” KATSEYE said.
The group said it was particularly excited about Daisy Chain Fields because of its focus on music, joy and community.
“We were especially excited for Daisy Chain Fields because it’s not just about music, but the greater mission of joy and community,” they added.
KATSEYE also sent its support to Rodrigo and the other performers, nonprofit organizations and volunteers involved in the event.
“We’re sending all our love to Olivia and to all of the incredible artists, non-profit organizations and volunteers who have given their time to make this day so special,” the group said.
“We’re sending all our love to Olivia and to all of the incredible artists, non-profit organizations and volunteers who have given their time to make this day so special,” the group said.
Following KATSEYE’s withdrawal, Devon Again was added to the festival lineup.
Megan’s injury comes at a difficult time for KATSEYE, which has already been navigating activities with a reduced lineup.

The group has continued performing without leader Sophia Laforteza, who announced earlier this month that she was taking a temporary hiatus to prioritize her mental health and well-being. Her return will be reassessed in September.
Sophia’s hiatus came months after Manon Bannerman also stepped away from group activities to focus on her health and well-being.
Before Megan’s injury, KATSEYE had been performing as a quartet consisting of Daniela Avanzini, Lara Raj, Megan and Yoonchae Jeung.

articles.title: Man arrested for stealing cop's car radiator in QC
articles.summary: Police arrested a 41-year-old man for allegedly stealing a car radiator worth P3,500 from the vehicle of a police officer in Barangay Maharlika, Quezon City, on Wednesday, Aug. 26. The suspect,…

blocks.text: Police recovered the car radiator allegedly stolen from a police officer's vehicle in Quezon City. (Photo courtesy of QCPD)
Police arrested a 41-year-old man for allegedly stealing a car radiator worth P3,500 from the vehicle of a police officer in Barangay Maharlika, Quezon City, on Wednesday, Aug. 26.
The suspect, identified only as alias “JM,” allegedly took the radiator from a vehicle parked outside an automotive service establishment on Mayon Street at around 9:20 p.m.
Police said the victim, a police officer, had brought his vehicle to the establishment for repair due to a defective radiator.
While the vehicle was being serviced, the victim temporarily placed the radiator on the cemented pavement outside the establishment before briefly going inside.
When he returned, he discovered that the radiator was missing.
The victim immediately sought assistance from personnel of the La Loma Police Station (PS 1), who were conducting patrol operations in the area.
The responding officers and the victim conducted a roving search in the vicinity, which led to the arrest of the suspect and recovery of the stolen radiator from his possession.

Police records showed that the suspect had a previous case for an alleged violation of Republic Act No. 10591, or the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act, in June 2024, and cases involving Presidential Decree No. 1602 (illegal gambling), Republic Act No. 10591 (firearms law), and City Ordinance No. 5121 (anti-deadly weapons measure) in April 2018.
The suspect is facing a theft charge before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office.

articles.title: Ilocos region logs 6 deaths due to leptospirosis
articles.summary: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — Six people have died from leptospirosis in the Ilocos Region since January, prompting the Department of Health (DOH) to warn residents against unnecessary contact with…

blocks.text: SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union — Six people have died from leptospirosis in the Ilocos Region since January, prompting the Department of Health (DOH) to warn residents against unnecessary contact with floodwaters amid continued rains.

The Regional Epidemiology and Surveillance Unit recorded 85 leptospirosis cases and six deaths from January 1 to August 8, 2026, with Pangasinan accounting for the most cases at 46, followed by La Union with 13, Ilocos Norte with 12, and Ilocos Sur and Dagupan City with six each.
Although the figure is 52 percent lower than the 177 cases recorded during the same period last year, the DOH said the deaths highlight the continuing danger posed by floodwater exposure.
“Floodwater exposure is not without risk, especially when there are wounds or breaks in the skin,” said Dr. Rheuel C. Bobis, head of the Regional Communicable Disease Cluster.

Leptospirosis is a potentially fatal bacterial infection caused by exposure to water or soil contaminated by the urine of infected animals, particularly rats. The bacteria can enter the body through cuts or wounds.

The DOH advised residents to avoid wading through floodwaters whenever possible. Those who cannot avoid exposure should wear waterproof boots, cover their wounds, and immediately wash exposed areas with soap and clean water.
Residents should seek medical attention if they develop fever, headache, muscle or calf pain, vomiting, chills, abdominal pain, red eyes, or yellowing of the skin or eyes after flood water exposure.
Bobis also warned against taking antibiotics such as doxycycline without medical advice, stressing that the need for preventive medication depends on the type and extent of exposure.
“Doxycycline is a prescription medicine,” he said, urging residents to consult the nearest health center for proper assessment.

articles.title: Alcaraz opens US Open title defense against Safiullin; Venus draws Kenin
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Carlos Alcaraz will open the defense of his U.S. Open title against an opponent who made a strong run at Wimbledon while the Spaniard was sidelined with an injury. Along with some…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Carlos Alcaraz will open the defense of his U.S. Open title against an opponent who made a strong run at Wimbledon while the Spaniard was sidelined with an injury.

Along with some interesting opening-round matches, the draws for men's and women's singles Thursday, Aug. 27, delivered one what-could-have-been possibility: Had Serena Williams decided to play, there could have been a Williams sisters showdown in Round 1.

When Venus Williams was given a wild card into the event at 46, the U.S. Tennis Association initially held one spot, which surely would have gone to Serena if the six-time U.S. Open champion wanted to play after returning to tennis for the first time since 2022. When the 44-year-old decided to only compete in doubles, the USTA awarded that last wild card over the weekend to American Sofia Kenin, the 2020 Australian Open champion.
On Thursday, Venus Williams and Kenin were randomly drawn to face each other.
Main draw play at the final Grand Slam tournament of the season begins Sunday.

Alcaraz is the No. 2 seed and will face Roman Safiullin. It will be Alcaraz's first singles match since April, after the two-time U.S. Open champion was forced to miss the French Open and Wimbledon because of a right wrist injury.

The Spaniard returned to play with Serena Williams in the mixed doubles tournament and looked rusty. He may have to be sharper against Safiullin, who reached the fourth round at Wimbledon, upsetting Andrey Rublev and Joao Fonseca along the way before falling to 24-time Grand Slam singles champion Novak Djokovic in four sets.
Safiullin also upset Alcaraz, ranked No. 2 at the time, in the ATP Masters 1000 in Paris in 2023. Alcaraz avenged that loss the following year at the Paris Olympics in their lone other meeting.
Alexander Zverev, the French Open champion who became the No. 1 seed in New York when Jannik Sinner pulled out with a knee injury, will open against Italian Lorenzo Sonego.

Two-time defending women's champion Aryna Sabalenka opens against Camila Osorio. The top-ranked Sabalenka, who has struggled during the North American hard-court season, could face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, the No. 6 seed, in the quarterfinals.

The other potential women's quarterfinals: No. 2 Elena Rybakina vs. No. 8 Iga Swiatek, and No. 4 Coco Gauff vs. No. 5 Mirra Andreeva, the French Open champion, in the bottom half; and No. 3 Jessica Pegula vs. No. 7 Karolina Muchova in Sabalenka's half.
Pegula, who opens against Elena-Gabriela Ruse, would play the Williams-Kenin winner in the second round.

The potential men's quarters: No. 1 Zverev vs. No. 6 Alex de Minaur, and No. 3 Felix Auger-Aliassime vs. No. 5 Flavio Cobolli in the top half; and No. 2 Alcaraz vs. No. 8 Ben Shelton, and No. 4 Djokovic vs. No. 7 Daniil Medvedev in the bottom half.
No. 10 seed Arthur Fils, coming off the title in the Cincinnati Open, faces two-time Grand Slam finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas, who was once ranked No. 3, in the first round.

Stan Wawrinka, the 2016 U.S. Open champion who received a wild card to play in his final Grand Slam tournament before retiring, faces Matteo Berrettini, the 2021 Wimbledon runner-up, to open a second straight major tournament. Berrettini won in four sets — all tiebreakers — at the All England Club. The winner would likely face Djokovic in the second round.

Rublev, the No. 23 seed, faces 2014 U.S. Open champion Marin Cilic. No. 13 Lorenzo Musetti, who reached the quarterfinals in New York last year, opens against Britain's Arthur Fery, who lost to Zverev in the Wimbledon semifinals.

Some first-round matches won't be determined until the conclusion of the qualifying tournaments, which were scheduled to finish Thursday before some matches were postponed until Friday because of rain. Potential women's contenders such as No. 11 Marta Kostyuk and No. 17 Alex Eala were among those waiting to see who they would face in their openers.

articles.title: 13-year-old boy faints after being forced to vape
articles.summary: Two men were arrested on Thursday, Aug. 27, after a 13-year-old boy lost consciousness after they allegedly forced him to use a vape in Pasig City. The Pasig City Police Station said the suspects,…

blocks.text: Two men were arrested on Thursday, Aug. 27, after a 13-year-old boy lost consciousness after they allegedly forced him to use a vape in Pasig City.

The Pasig City Police Station said the suspects, identified as “Kurt,” 23, and “Fogata,” 18, were apprehended in Barangay Manggahan by virtue of a warrant of arrest issued by the Family Court Branch 12 in Pasig City on Aug. 25.
Police said the suspects were accused of violating Republic Act No. 7610, or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act, with recommended of P80,000.

The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the mother of the victim, who claimed that the suspects forced the minor to use a vape, causing him to experience dizziness and subsequently lose consciousness.
The police did not provide further details on the minor’s condition.

Col. Hendrix B. Mangaldan, Pasig City police chief, said the arrest of the suspects highlighted the importance of sustained law enforcement efforts in safeguarding children and protecting them from all forms of abuse, exploitation, and discrimination.

“The Pasig City Police Station remains steadfast in its commitment to upholding the law, protecting the vulnerable, and ensuring a safe and secure community through intensified law enforcement operations and the effective implementation of warrants of arrest,” the station said.

In 2024, Dr. Maria Encarnita Blanco-Limpin of the Philippine College of Chest Physicians and the Philippine Medical Association said electronic smoking devices available in the country include Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS), Electronic Non-Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENNDS), and Heated Tobacco Products (HTPs).
Vaping, which falls under ENDS, involves inhaling and exhaling an aerosol produced by an e-cigarette or similar device.
She noted that vape products may contain chemicals that are toxic and carcinogenic.
Among the immediate health risks of vaping are airway irritation, which may cause coughing and shortness of breath.
Vaping may also contribute to cardiovascular problems and chronic respiratory diseases.

articles.title: UP Visayas' 1st chancellor dies at 105
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY— Dr. Dionisia A. Rola, the first chancellor of the University of the Philippines (UP Visayas) has died at the age of 105. The UP Visayas announced that Rola passed away on Wednesday…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY— Dr. Dionisia A. Rola, the first chancellor of the University of the Philippines (UP Visayas) has died at the age of 105.
The UP Visayas announced that Rola passed away on Wednesday evening, August 26.
Rola was a formidable force in the existence of UP in Iloilo when she started her career after UP Iloilo College (UPIC) was established in July 1947.

By the 1970s, Rola became the dean of the UP College Iloilo (UPCI) and envisioned the creation of an autonomous UP unit in the Visayas with its main campus in Miag-ao, a coastal town in Iloilo province.

“She lobbied for the creation of a new autonomous campus in the Visayas, requested a loan from the World Bank, and held coordination activities with concerned officials at the national and local levels for the lot acquisition,” the UP Visayas stated.
It was in 1980 when Executive Order No. 628 formally operationalized UP in the Visayas and Rola became its first chancellor.
Rola also had the distinction of becoming the first woman chancellor in the entire UP System.
Rola also established key arts and cultural programs for the university. It was through her initiatives that the Center for West Visayan Studies (CWVS) was created in June 1975.
Rola was also the brains behind what is now the UP Visayas Museum of Art and Cultural Heritage (MACH).
“Chancellor Rola helped shape UP Visayas into an institution committed to honor, excellence, service, and regional development,” stated the UP Visayas Alumni Association.
