articles.title: Meta settles lawsuit for $18 billion
articles.summary: Meta, the owner of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and messaging app WhatsApp, has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle with the lawsuit filed against them across 29 US…

blocks.text: Meta, the owner of social media platforms Facebook, Instagram, Threads, and messaging app WhatsApp, has agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle with the lawsuit filed against them across 29 US states.
The lawsuit alleged that Meta built their platforms to be addictive for children, even as it caused harm and impact of social media on them.

The amount 18 billion seems more like a slap to the wrist, since Meta has earned 200 billion last year. It is also the price they are willing to pay to not move the lawsuit into a jury trial. A jury trial would have meant a group of chosen ordinary citizens must listen to the facts of a trial and evaluate evidence presented, and it is them who will make a verdict. Whereas a settlement is where both parties have agreed to an outcome.

This is not a problem isolated within the digital walls of Meta alone, and Meta knows it. They posted a call to action to TikTok and YouTube to join them in protecting teens. It was the most “If we’re going down, you’re going down with me” kind of thing.

Developed with 52 state attorney generals, Meta will launch a set of protections, which include adding time limits on social media use, showing daily usage analytics, and prompts to encourage “intentional” use. That last one may mean encouraging teens to use social media only when they actually need to and not simply open the app and start doomscrolling.

Other protections include blocking notifications on times when the teens are supposed to be in school. Also, blocking the number of likes and reactions from their posts and others’ posts. “Extreme makeup filters” will also be blocked.
Meta will also invest in improving their age verification.

articles.title: SuperManila Comic Con celebrates Filipino komiks legends with two exclusive classics
articles.summary: Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks. This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage…

blocks.text: Lifestyle | Luminaries and Life
Limited-edition releases of "Darna" and "Kaluluwa ni Dante" bring iconic works of Mars Ravelo and Francisco V. Coching closer to collectors
Before superheroes conquered movie screens and streaming platforms, their adventures lived in the pages of Filipino komiks.
(Photos: SuperManila Comic Con)

This September, SuperManila Comic Con 2026 celebrates that rich heritage with two highly collectible exclusive releases: “Classic Darna #1,” featuring the earliest adventures of Mars Ravelo's legendary heroine, and “Kaluluwa ni Dante,” a landmark masterpiece by the "King of Komiks," Francisco V. Coching.

Available exclusively at SuperManila Comic Con, these special editions allow longtime fans to revisit two Philippine comics classics while introducing their timeless stories and artwork to a new generation of collectors.
"Classic Darna #1" (in color and sepia) created by Mars Ravelo, illustrated by Nestor Redondo, exclusive cover artwork by Stanley "Artgerm" Lau
‘Classic Darna #1’: The legend returns!
Created by legendary Filipino komiks writer Mars Ravelo, Darna first appeared in Pilipino Komiks in 1950 and went on to become one of the Philippines' most enduring cultural icons.

“Classic Darna #1” SuperManila Comic Con Exclusive reprints stories from Darna's earliest komiks appearances, including her first appearance and legendary origin story. The original stories feature the breathtaking artwork of acclaimed Filipino artist Nestor Redondo, whose illustrations helped define Darna's iconic look for generations of readers.
Adding a stunning contemporary touch to this historic release, both editions feature exclusive cover artwork by internationally renowned artist Stanley "Artgerm" Lau.
The release comes in two strictly limited editions:

items: Full-Color Virgin Cover Edition — ₱1,000 per copy, 1,000 copies featuring the original stories presented in vibrant color.

Sepia Cover / Black-and-White Interior Edition — ₱800 per copy, 1,000 copies featuring a sepia-toned cover and the stories reproduced in black and white, paying tribute to the way generations of Filipino readers experienced Darna in the pages of komiks.

blocks.text: Every copy of both editions also includes an exclusive Darna trading card.
This is not a new story or retelling, but a reprint of the classic material that helped establish Darna's enduring legacy.
"Kaluluwa ni Dante" by Francisco V. Coching, the "King of Komiks," 116-page softcover edition, original black-and-white format, only 300 copies (₱1,000 per copy)
‘Kaluluwa ni Dante’: A masterpiece from the ‘King of Komiks’

Francisco V. Coching (1919–1998) is widely regarded as one of the greatest storytellers and illustrators in Philippine comics history. Hailed as the "King of Komiks," Coching created more than 50 serialized komiks novels over a career spanning four decades, including such celebrated works as “Pedro Penduko,” “Hagibis,” “Sabas, ang Barbaro,” “El Indio,” “Lapu-Lapu,” and “Kaluluwa ni Dante.”

First serialized in 1949, “Kaluluwa ni Dante” follows Dante Magtanggol on an extraordinary out-of-body journey guided by the mysterious Dr. Futiphar. Blending mystery, fantasy, adventure, and moral drama, the story explores justice, redemption, love, and the timeless struggle between good and evil.
With Coching's richly detailed artwork and cinematic storytelling, “Kaluluwa ni Dante” remains one of his most celebrated masterpieces.

Coching's influence extended far beyond komiks. Fifty-one of his 63 komiks novels were adapted into films, making him one of the most adapted creators in Philippine cinema. In 2014, he was posthumously conferred the title of National Artist for Visual Arts.
SuperManila Comic Con presents a special 116-page softcover edition of "Kaluluwa ni Dante," faithfully reproduced in its original black-and-white format, preserving Coching's timeless artwork.
Only 300 copies will be produced, making this a particularly rare opportunity for collectors and fans of Philippine komiks history.
Two legends. Two classics. One celebration of Philippine comics.

From “Darna,” the legendary heroine created by Mars Ravelo, to “Kaluluwa ni Dante,” the masterpiece of National Artist Francisco V. Coching, these exclusive SuperManila Comic Con releases celebrate the creators and stories that helped shape Filipino pop culture.

“Classic Darna #1” and “Kaluluwa ni Dante” will be available exclusively at the SMCC Merch Booth at The Concourse during SuperManila Comic Con 2026, from Sept. 4 to 6, 2026, at The Concourse and Space at One Ayala, Makati City.
For tickets and event updates, visit supermanila.ph and follow SuperManila Comic Con on its official social media channels.

articles.title: Westmincom marks 20th anniversary
articles.summary: ZAMBOANGA CITY- The Western Mindanao Command marked its 20th founding anniversary on Thursday, August 27, at the gymnasium of Camp Don Basilio Navarro here with the theme "Strengthening Joint and…

blocks.text: ZAMBOANGA CITY- The Western Mindanao Command marked its 20th founding anniversary on Thursday, August 27, at the gymnasium of Camp Don Basilio Navarro here with the theme "Strengthening Joint and Inter-Agency Operations toward Resilient Western MIndanao."

The ceremony, graced by AFP Chief of Staff Gen. Antonio Nafarrete, brought together military personnel, government officials, partner agencies, veterans and other stakeholders to recognize two decades of service and sacrifice.

The program featured a live simulation exercise showcasing inter-agency defense operations. Awards were also given to officers, enlisted personnel, the Civilian Human Resource of the Year and other stakeholders in recognition of their contributions to the command.
The anniversary was the culmination of a series of activities including the Run-for-a Cause, Veterans’ Day, Interagency Territorial Defense Operations exercises, a wellness caravan, and others.
Maj. Gen. Jose Vladimir R. Cagara, acting commander of WESMINCOM, said the milestone also provides an opportunity to assess the command’s readiness amid an evolving security environment.
“Today, we celebrate 20 years of service, sacrifice, protecting our people, preserving peace, and defending this part of the nation,” Cagara said.

General Nafarrete thanked stakeholders for their continued support to WestMinCom and its units. He said the command will play a greater role this year in coordinating and harmonizing security efforts, strengthening communication and promoting a peaceful and orderly election process in coordination with the Philippine National Police and other government agencies.

The celebration underscored the continuing partnership among the military, government agencies, and local communities in protecting peace gains and building safer and more resilient communities across Western MIndanao.

articles.title: Gokongwei takes PhilWeb helm amid AI gaming pivot
articles.summary: Tycoon Lance Y. Gokongwei has been named chairman of the board of directors of PhilWeb Corp. to mark the gaming company’s shift to a supplier of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled online gaming…

blocks.text: Tycoon Lance Y. Gokongwei has been named chairman of the board of directors of PhilWeb Corp. to mark the gaming company’s shift to a supplier of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled online gaming platforms to some of the country’s biggest casinos.

In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Friday, Aug. 28, PhilWeb said its board of directors approved the relinquishment by Crisanto Roy B. Alcid of his positions as chairman of the board and chief executive officer (CEO) of the corporation, effective Aug. 27, 2026. He will continue to serve as a director of the corporation.
The board also approved the appointment of Gokongwei, already a director of PhilWeb, as chairman of the board, effective Aug. 27, to serve for the remainder of Alcid’s term.

In a separate disclosure, the company said Gokongwei now directly owns 159.53 million shares, equivalent to a 15-percent stake, acquired at ₱8 apiece or a total of ₱2 billion pursuant to the share purchase agreement (SPA) executed last month.

PhilWeb said in a statement that this leadership transition completes the company’s governance restructuring, following Gokongwei’s recent ₱2.02-billion strategic equity investment and his appointment to the board in July.

It noted that the election signals PhilWeb’s definitive shift from capitalization to the aggressive, large-scale execution of its commercial online-led business-to-business (B2B) AI-enabled technology roadmap.

“This transition marks a critical inflection point for our capitalization and operational scale. Our objective is clear: to deploy institutional-grade, AI-powered infrastructure that establishes a new operational standard for security and compliance across the regulated digital ecosystem,” said Gokongwei.

Under Gokongwei’s strategic oversight, PhilWeb is accelerating the deployment of its enterprise AI layer. This technological pivot transitions the company into an institutional-grade digital gaming solutions provider.

The immediate operational mandate focuses on the integration of real-time operational monitoring, algorithmic risk management, regulatory compliance automation, anti-fraud detection, and data-driven customer lifecycle optimization.

“Having Lance Gokongwei step into the chairman role provides the institutional governance required for our next phase of scale. His strategic oversight ensures that our AI infrastructure rollout—specifically engineered to serve the complex backend needs of luxury integrated casino resorts and global platform providers—is executed with absolute capital market discipline,” said PhilWeb President Brian Ng.
The governance upgrade strengthens PhilWeb’s position as the foundational operational backbone for the regulated digital gaming sector.

The company’s AI-driven technology currently powers a premier, interconnected ecosystem of luxury integrated casino resorts and licensed operators, including Okada Manila, Hann Casino, Newport World Resorts, NUSTAR Resort and Casino, FBM Philippines, and PT Gaming.

Furthermore, PhilWeb continues to embed elite global content providers, such as Pragmatic Play and Games Global, into its unified digital infrastructure, securing deep commercial moats and operational dominance in the B2B market. - James A. Loyola

articles.title: Good Good out as PGA Tour title sponsor, Callaway deal ends
articles.summary: ATLANTA (AP) — Good Good Golf lost its partnership with Callaway on Thursday, Aug. 27, and no longer will be title sponsor of a PGA Tour event in November as the fallout continued over a video for a…

blocks.text: ATLANTA (AP) — Good Good Golf lost its partnership with Callaway on Thursday, Aug. 27, and no longer will be title sponsor of a PGA Tour event in November as the fallout continued over a video for a new Callaway driver that showed a man shoving a woman to the ground who was trying to touch the golf club.

Good Good, among the most popular in the YouTube Golf space, has said the video was meant to be a spinoff from the movie, “Obsession.” But the criticism was immediate and relentless, and the pressure began mounting by the day.
The video was deleted the same day it was posted on Aug. 20, but it continued to make the rounds on social media and apologies from Good Good and Callaway had little effect.
“We were disappointed with what we saw,” PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp said Tuesday of the response from Good Good. He said its role as a title sponsor was a “fluid situation.”

“We agree with their decision to use this time to focus on their organization and the work ahead,” the tour said in a statement Thursday. “The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all.”
The tournament already was changed on the PGA Tour's website to “Austin Championship.”

Golf Channel postponed a Good Good reality show Wednesday — “Big Break x Good Good” — because a sponsor, reported to be Galaxy Golf, wanted its brand scrubbed from the telecast. Dick's Sporting Goods removed the apparel from its stories. And then Callaway said it was ending the three-year sponsorship.
The PGA Tour confirmed Good Good said it would pull out as title sponsor of the new Nov. 12-15 tournament in Austin, Texas. The tour said the tournament still would be played.

“After thoughtful discussions with the PGA Tour and careful reflection, we have decided to step away as sponsor of the tour event in Austin this fall,” Good Good said in a social media post. “We recognize that we have work to do as an organization, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we will learn from this situation.”
Golf Channel announced Friday afternoon the Big Break x Good Good series would be scrapped this year. The winner was to have received a sponsor exemption to the Austin tournament.

“Following recent developments involving Good Good, and including the fact that the intended outcome of the series can no longer be fulfilled, Golf Channel will not be able to complete this season of Big Break as planned,” Golf Channel said in a statement.
It said Big Break would return next year.

In the 60-second video for Callaway’s new driver co-branded with Good Good, Garrett Clark shoves Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she reaches for the driver. As she is on the ground he leans over tells her, "Do not touch my new driver.”
Clark and Miestowski work for Good Good.

The video was pulled the night it was posted, and it was followed by apologies by Good Good Golf and Callaway Golf the next day. But then Callaway added another layer of apologies, this one from CEO Chip Brewer, who conceded that while Good Good produced the video, Callaway approved it before it was posted.
Brewer said the approval never should have happened and the company would investigate.

Callaway posted to its social media channels on Thursday that it has ended its relationship with Good Good effective immediately; has taken “appropriate internal corrective actions” and strengthened approval procedures to avoid another mistake; and has committed $1 million to support organizations working to prevent violence against women.
“These actions do not undo the harm caused or excuse our role in it,” the statement said. “We sincerely apologize to everyone who was hurt, disappointed, or offended by this incident.”

Good Good Golf was launched as a YouTube channel in 2020 and now is among the largest content creators in the sport, featuring eight men and four women competing in golf and various challenges. It has made-for-TV shows, apparel and other merchandise.
Clark, one of the Good Good founders, posted an eight-minute video Wednesday evening in which he called it “the worst ad known to man” and the reaction to the ad was “not what we stand for.”
“I do not support DV (domestic violence) or abuse or any of that of any kind," he said.
The PGA Tour has embraced such content creators over the last several years, even staging exhibitions during the week of The Players Championship and Tour Championship.

articles.title: Escudero: Free housing through government land usufruct will benefit millions of low-income Filipinos
articles.summary: Millions of low-income Filipinos stand to benefit on a proposed law that seeks to institutionalize free housing through usufruct, a legal arrangement that grants families the right to occupy and…

blocks.text: Millions of low-income Filipinos stand to benefit on a proposed law that seeks to institutionalize free housing through usufruct, a legal arrangement that grants families the right to occupy and enjoy government land and housing without owning them.

Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero pointed this out when he endorsed Senate Bill No. 2421 or the Free Housing Through Usufruct Act under Committee Report No. 79 on Wednesday, August 26. The bill is now pending second reading.

“Through usufruct, this bill seeks to grant Filipino families the right to occupy, use, and enjoy government land and improvements for residential purposes, while ownership remains with the State,” Escudero said of the measure.

Under the bill, only underprivileged, homeless citizens who do not own real property and have no affiliation with squatting syndicates will qualify, the chairman of the Senate Committee on Urban Planning, Housing and Resettlement further said.
Each usufruct agreement, Escudero said, will be covered by a written contract detailing rights and obligations, including maintenance of the property and payment of utilities.

“Section 5 outlines who may benefit from adequate and decent housing under this proposal: underprivileged Filipinos who do not own a home or real property, and who are not professional squatters or members of squatting syndicates,” Escudero said.

Under the bill, the housing units are strictly for residential use and warned that occupants cannot sell, transfer, mortgage, or rent out the units to others—acts that will cancel their right to use the property and ban them from government housing program for 10 years.
SB 2421 also requires registration of usufruct contracts with the Registry of Deeds, ensuring transparency and legal protection for beneficiaries.

Under the measure, the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) will monitor the implementation, while local government units (LGUs) will be tasked to manage properties and guarantee access to basic services.
Escudero said the bill is designed to prevent abuse while securing tenure for genuine beneficiaries.
“Each usufruct agreement is embodied in a written contract specifying the parties' rights and obligations, as well as the conditions for the continued use and enjoyment of the property,” he said.
According to the senator, the concept of usufruct dates back to Roman civil law but remains relevant today as a tool to address the persistent problem of homelessness.
“If usufruct is the right to use a property and enjoy its fruits, may this proposal yield adequate and decent housing for the millions of Filipinos in need,” he emphasized.

articles.title: Celebrating 20 years of local craft as Padday na Lima builds a sustainable future
articles.summary: Cagayan Valley’s vibrant craftsmanship, flavors, and entrepreneurial spirit have arrived in Alabang as the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Region 2 opened the 20th Padday na Lima Regional…

blocks.text: Cagayan Valley’s vibrant craftsmanship, flavors, and entrepreneurial spirit have arrived in Alabang as the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Region 2 opened the 20th Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair last Aug. 24, 2026, at Festival Mall. With more than 100 micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the region’s five provinces, this milestone fair invites shoppers to discover products that are proudly local and thoughtfully made with sustainability in mind.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

Carrying the theme “20 Years of Vibrant Hands: Crafting a Sustainable Legacy of Culture and Community,” this year’s Padday na Lima goes beyond showcasing products as it celebrates the hands, stories, skills, and communities that make them possible. From regional delicacies and handcrafted pieces to fashion, home products, and other unique finds, visitors can experience the many ways Cagayan Valley’s local enterprises are creating value while keeping culture and sustainability alive.

The celebration drew distinguished guests, including DTI Undersecretary Blesila A. Lantayona and Muntinlupa City Mayor Hon. Rozzano Rufino B. Biazon. Meanwhile, First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos and the PLGUs of Batanes, Cagayan, and Isabela conveyed their support for the trade fair. DTI Region 2 Regional Director Ma. Sofia G. Narag, CESO V, and Acting Assistant Regional Director Atty. Michael B. Paggabao welcomed them all to the celebration, along with other partners and guests.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

The Padday na Lima Website 2.0 was also relaunched, giving MSMEs another avenue to bring their products to customers through digital commerce. Meanwhile, DTI Region 2 and the Department of Tourism launched Lakbay Likha: A Creative Tourism Experience, opening new possibilities for local products and craftsmanship by connecting them with the region’s tourism destinations and experiences.

The spotlight also shone on enterprises making a difference through the Padday na Lima MSME Awards, which recognized businesses demonstrating innovation and sustainability. Adding flair to the celebration, the 20th Padday na Lima Fashion Show, “Hibla’t Habi ng Rehiyon Dos: Padday na Lima Collections,” transformed local materials and traditional craftsmanship into contemporary fashion under the creative direction of Nueva Vizcaya-born designer and Region 2 Creative Icon Michael Barassi.

blocks.caption: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

blocks.text: (Photo: Padday na Lima Regional Trade Fair)

The opening festivities culminated in a ceremonial bamboo tapping and the launch of the Padday na Lima Song, followed by an exhibit tour that officially opened the seven-day fair to shoppers and visitors.

For 20 years, Padday na Lima has been bringing Cagayan Valley closer to wider markets while helping sustain the people, skills, traditions, and livelihoods behind every product. Now, it’s your turn to experience it. Visit Padday na Lima at Festival Mall until Aug. 30, 2026, and discover your next local favorite. Come and take home a piece of Cagayan Valley’s vibrant and sustainable story.

articles.title: Court rejects Tarlac lawmaker Rivera’s bid to consolidate 9 graft cases
articles.summary: 'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
Jansen Romero/Rappler
'Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,' the anti-graft court says

items: The Sandiganbayan court rejected Representative Noel Rivera's request to consolidate his graft cases, citing that they involve different public works projects.
Rivera is accused of having an unlawful interest in Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which secured significant government contracts during his congressional term.
The court emphasized that consolidating the cases could lead to confusion and delays, as they involve separate contracts and are spread across multiple divisions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The anti-graft court Sandiganbayan has rejected Tarlac 3rd District Representative Noel Rivera’s bid to have his graft cases handled by just one court division, saying these involve different public works projects and that lumping them together could cause confusion and delays.

In two separate resolutions on Thursday, August 27, the Sandiganbayan’s 6th Division denied Rivera’s motion for consolidation. The ruling, made by associate justices Sarah Jane Fernandez, Kevin Narce Vivero and Lord Villanueva, rejected the congressman’s contention that the nine cases were similar and that having only one division handle them would save time and resources.

Rivera is accused of keeping an unlawful interest in the construction firm Tarlac 3-G Construction and Development Corporation, which bagged government projects worth millions of pesos while he was serving as a member of the House of Representatives.

blocks.caption: Congress, contractors, conflict, corruption: A list of Rappler exclusives

blocks.text: Rivera has been accused by Ombudsman Boying Remulla of being one of the so-called “congtractors,” or members of the House of Representatives who keep stakes in companies that bagged juicy public works contracts.
Prosecutors have also accused him of owning a 54.8% stake in Tarlac 3-G, while his wife, Evelyn, allegedly held another 45%.
An earlier Rappler report cited DPWH data showing that Tarlac 3-G had already been winning a large share of government projects in Tarlac even before Rivera became a congressman.
Since Rivera entered Congress, Tarlac 3-G has secured P671 million worth of DPWH projects. The company reported total assets of P392 million in its 2024 financial statement.
Rivera’s cases were spread across six Sandiganbayan divisions, with the 5th, 6th and 7th divisions handling two cases each, while the 1st, 2nd and 4th divisions each took on one.
The court stressed that there was little chance of conflicting rulings because the cases involved separate contracts.

The cases involve contracts that Tarlac 3-G secured while Rivera was already serving as a congressman, with eight coming from the DPWH, while the Philippine State College of Aeronautics awarded the remaining contract.
“Instead of expediting the proceedings, consolidation will merely cause delay,” read part of the Sandiganbayan ruling. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Eala, seeded No. 17, takes on qualifier at US Open first round
articles.summary: Alex Eala is ready to take the US Open by storm as the No. 17 seed -- her highest-ever Grand Slam seeding -- clashes with a qualifier at Flushing Meadows. Her historic seeding, surpassing her…

blocks.text: Alex Eala is ready to take the US Open by storm as the No. 17 seed -- her highest-ever Grand Slam seeding -- clashes with a qualifier at Flushing Meadows.

Her historic seeding, surpassing her previous No. 25 mark at Wimbledon, places her in the bottom half of a loaded draw packed with dangerous elite opponents standing in her path that include last year’s finalist and 10th seed Amanda Anisimova.
A first-round victory would arrange the 21-year-old Filipina star a duel with the winner between Oleksandra Oliynykova of Ukraine and wildcard Reese Brantmeier of the United States.
Eala recently faced Oliynykova at the WTA 500 event in Strasbourg, France last May, falling to the Ukrainian in a three-set battle in the opening round.
The Filipina, however, has never faced Brantmeier on the WTA tour.

Other notable potential opponents for Eala deeper in the draw are good friend and 14th seed Iva Jovic, two-time Grand Slam doubles quarterfinalist Anastasia Potapova, 2017 French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko and 19-year-old reigning French Open champion Mirra Andreeva.
Of course, no path is easy at any Grand Slam as Eala is expected to go all out to eclipse her best Grand Slam showing of a fourth-round finish at the Wimbledon a few months ago.

Eala is carrying the momentum of an impressive North American swing campaign where she captured her breakthrough WTA title at the Mubadala DC Open, slaying giants like Zheng Qinwen, last year's champion Leylah Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka and 2024 US Open finalist Jessica Pegula.
She is also coming off a mixed doubles stint with Canadian Felix Auger-Aliassime, where they lost to spouses Gael Monfils and Svitolina.

articles.title: ‘Habagat’ to bring heavy rains during long weekend — PAGASA
articles.summary: Those looking forward to the long weekend may have to adjust their plans as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of the country, particularly western Luzon.…

blocks.text: Those looking forward to the long weekend may have to adjust their plans as the southwest monsoon or “habagat” is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of the country, particularly western Luzon.

Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) weather specialist Obet Badrina said Friday, Aug. 28 that significant rainfall may prevail over Ilocos Region, Bataan, Zambales, parts of Calabarzon, Metro Manila, Oriental Mindoro, and Occidental Mindoro.
Heavy rains are expected to continue through Saturday, Aug. 29, and Sunday, Aug. 30, although they may ease by Sunday afternoon or Monday, Aug. 31, National Heroes Day.

“Partikular na sa Sabado at Linggo, inaasahan natin na magiging tuloy-tuloy ang mga malalakas na pag-ulan. Posibleng mabawasan po yan bandang hapon ng Linggo o Lunes na. Kaya sa mga kababayan natin na may activity this coming long weekend ay consider nating yung ineexpect na mga malalakas na pag-ulan lalong-lalo na sa western section nga ng western section ng Luzon (We expect the heavy rains to continue particularly on Saturday and Sunday. These may ease by Sunday afternoon or Monday. Those with activities this coming long weekend should consider the expected heavy rains, particularly over western Luzon),” Badrina said.
The rest of Luzon and Visayas may have scattered rains and thunderstorms, while Mindanao may generally have partly cloudy skies with isolated rain showers or thunderstorms.
The low-pressure area (LPA), designated LPA 08i, was enhancing the habagat as it was located 720 kilometers east of Itbayat, Batanes as of 3 a.m. Friday.
The LPA could still develop into a tropical cyclone this weekend but is not expected to make landfall in the Philippines.

“Posible pa rin ito maging bagyo this coming weekend pero hindi na ito magkakaroon ng direktang epekto sa ating bansa. Hindi ito inaasahang maglandfall sa Pilipinas at ang magiging direksyon nitong low-pressure area na kung sakaling maging bagyo ay sa may bahagi naman ng Taiwan (It is still possible for this to become a tropical cyclone this coming weekend, but it will no longer have a direct effect on our country. It is not expected to make landfall in the Philippines, and if it becomes a tropical cyclone, the low-pressure area is expected to move toward Taiwan),” Badrina said.
If LPA 08i develops into a tropical depression, it will be given the local name “Pilandok.”
Another LPA could form next week and may further strengthen the habagat, Badrina said, citing PAGASA’s two-week tropical cyclone threat potential forecast.

“Around August 27 to September 2, inaasahan na ang low-pressure area na ating minomonitor ay patungo sa bahagi ng Taiwan. Samantala, by next week posibleng may mabuo na panibagong low-pressure area at maaaring magpatuloy na magpalakas ng habagat hanggang next week (Around August 27 to September 2, the low-pressure area we are monitoring is expected to move toward Taiwan. Meanwhile, by next week, another low-pressure area may form and could continue to strengthen the habagat into next week),” Badrina said.
He advised the public to continue monitoring PAGASA updates as longer-range forecasts are less certain and may still change.

blocks.text: There is something about spring that makes everything feel possible again. For Gucci, that sense of renewal becomes the starting point of its latest campaign, Gucci Primavera—the first campaign unveiled under the creative direction of Demna.

Celebrating rebirth through the transformative power of love, the campaign brings together a stellar global cast of 10 talents from across entertainment, fashion, music, and sport, with Asian representation taking center stage.

Chinese actor Xiao Zhan joins South Korean stars Jin of BTS and Ningning of Aespa, alongside acclaimed actress Lee Young Ae and model and rapper Tarzzan. The global lineup continues with Canadian singer Shawn Mendes, American model Alex Consani, football icon Tom Brady, rapper Rico Nasty, and British rapper EsDeeKid—a deliberately eclectic group that reflects the many facets of Gucci’s evolving identity.

Photographed by Michal Chelbin, the talents appear in looks from Demna’s debut Gucci collection, introducing a new vocabulary of silhouettes and textures. There is an ease to the styling, with pieces designed to move across different modes of dressing while retaining the house’s unmistakable codes. Heritage is present, but it feels reframed rather than revisited—a contemporary interpretation of Gucci through Demna’s lens.
And then there is love.

Bringing the campaign’s emotional narrative to life is a short film featuring fashion icon Kate Moss, who lip-syncs to Chris Isaak’s haunting “Wicked Game.” The visuals are romantic, slightly surreal, and deliberately cinematic, a fitting introduction to a campaign built around the idea of awakening. Much like spring itself, Gucci Primavera is about what happens when something dormant begins to stir: new energy, new encounters, and the possibility of falling in love all over again.

articles.title: Psychologists want us to rethink what we ask about school violence
articles.summary: Rather than neatly condense all the violence and trace it to one root cause, psychologists choose to ask the difficult questions about each individual case. Each child in conflict with the law is not…

blocks.text: This is Part 1 of a two-part story.

The kids aren’t alright. Only a few months into the school year, multiple cases of school violence have been reported throughout the Philippines, where the students themselves are the perpetrators inflicting harm on their school community. The most recent incident in Zamboanga was a school shooting that resulted in the death of two students: one who was fatally shot by his schoolmate, while the other was the shooter himself, who, after live streaming his violent acts on social media, ended his own life.

These incidents have alarmed psychologists and mental health practitioners, especially those who work with minors and young Filipinos. But rather than neatly condense all the violence and attribute it to one root cause, they choose to ask the difficult questions about each individual case. They want to understand each student not just as a perpetrator, but as a highly vulnerable person.

“When I heard about the school violence, I immediately asked, ‘What was happening to the teenager’s life that made her or him to be in that position?’” said psychologist Jannah Trixie Cuevas. “What was happening at home? What was happening in the school? Why did it happen in school? What comes to their mind before they started getting the gun? Did someone influence them? Did someone try to manipulate them?”

“No student will do that if they can handle things properly,” psychologist Arnel Sarte Jr. said. “We have to ask: What are they experiencing that pushed them to do that? What are they carrying on their own, until they reach a breaking point?”

Both Cuevas and Sarte work with Sapphire Clinics East Inc., a Filipino-owned rehabilitation and psychological services network in Metro Manila. In the two years they have been operating, the clinic has already handled more than 2,700 clients with a median age of 14 years old. In their work, they respond to warning signs in children and minors who exhibit mental health issues in order to prevent any “breaking points” from happening.

As minors, children and teenagers’ brains are not yet fully developed. Their prefrontal cortex, the part of their brain which manages decision making, emotion processing and control, and impulse regulation, will only fully mature around their mid-20s. Until then, they are “like sponges,” absorbing everything around them.

“Anything that they’re experiencing at school, at home, also what they’re seeing online, they will absorb quickly. Imagine all the risks that they can absorb while they’re growing up,” Sarte said. “If they’re exposed to bullying, invalidation, pressure, that can make them do things they don’t want to. As kids, their brain isn’t fully developed. They don’t have enough ways to properly process things.”

Processing difficult experiences and complex emotions with children is crucial for parents and schools. It is what will save their children from internalizing and carrying their struggles on their own to the point where they cannot bear it anymore. Once a child reaches a breaking point, they can either implode or explode; they can hurt themselves or hurt others.

In schools, experts say teachers and administrators are becoming more observant and attuned to the mental health warning signs and calls for help their students are exhibiting. Hannah Pellejo Jara, CEO and founder of Sapphire Clinics East, says that educational institutions have been partnering with them for more mental health support for their students because there are times when the school is no longer equipped to handle them.

“What they’re saying is there’s really a shift with the mental health of children,” she shared. “In their guidance office, they have concerns. That’s why they’re partnering with us. What we have seen are suicidal cases, depression cases. A lot of it is family conflict, I would say. We’re seeing a lot of anxiety, panic, and anger management, even in kids.”

Questions that seem reasonable to ask about this situation are, “Why are they like that?” or “What’s wrong with them?” But psychologists propose more productive questions that avoid connotations of defectiveness or blaming the child for things they perhaps could not control. “What are they going through?” “What is their family history like?” or “What did they experience?” are questions that instead seek to understand the child and see them as a whole person.
Guided by the biopsychosocial model, psychologists check the different dimensions of the child to understand their mental health vulnerabilities.

First is the biological factor, specifically their genes, brain chemistry, hormones, and overall physical health. Is their family vulnerable to mental health disorders? Is there a predisposition toward violence or issues like impulse control?

blocks.caption: [OPINION] If our answer starts at the school gate, we are too late

blocks.text: Second is the psychological factor. If they’re vulnerable to certain disorders, are they prone to being sensitive and emotionally or mentally overwhelmed? Are they moody? How do they cope with struggles and conflict? Do they have triggers?

Third, the social factor. What is their environment like at home? At school? Who are their support systems? Who are their friends? Do they feel supported and validated? What is their family’s socioeconomic situation?
The answers to these questions are the puzzle pieces that form the bigger picture of what burdens a person and has built up inside them.

“For a certain person to develop a disorder, there should be an interaction with the genes, the predispositions, and the social factors or environmental factors that would really nurture the disorder,” Cuevas said. “For example, you cannot inherit gambling itself, but the problems when it comes to impulse control. And then, you get connected with people who usually have problems when it comes to impulse control. It creates more tendencies to develop, but it’s not a guarantee.”

Children with mental health vulnerabilities might not even develop disorders if they have access to adequate support systems and safe spaces at home and in their immediate community. “Sometimes what happens is that they just get worse when the environment, when the kid is repeatedly exposed to triggers,” said Sarte.
What could these triggering environments look like?

“There could be a lot of invalidations at home, a lot of unprocessed [experiences] at home, a lot of negative emotions inside the home that teenagers no longer feel safe at home, I think some part of it is when there’s a lot of violence inside the home,” Cuevas said as examples, looking back on past anxiety, depression, and trauma cases.

These environments normalize aggression and violence and elicit stress over feeling unsafe. “Even though we think that the kids don’t have any reaction to it, something is going on with their minds,” Cuevas warned. “Especially teenagers, this is the age that they are making sense of what’s happening in the world. As they’re making sense of the world, it was normalized to just shout at people, to just be aggressive to people, to just not talk when things are not going well at home. It usually starts with that.”

One effect this has on children can result in mirrored behavior, where a kid mirrors the violence at home by bullying others. Another is the child developing a persistent sense of helplessness, of feeling small and defenseless against those harming them.
Cuevas is worried, however, by how children who experience helplessness could perceive the school violence cases, especially the live streamed Zamboanga shooting.

“For some kids who feel very helpless, very small of themselves, seeing this all over the social media for two to three days, maybe one week, gives them an idea. ‘Oh, I can do it too. For them, for me to feel more powerful,’ that gives them a sense of power again.”

She echoed the calls of fellow psychologists at the Psychological Association of the Philippines for social media users and members of the media to be responsible about their coverage of the incidents, especially with the risk of copycat behavior.

“The child who feels helpless, upon seeing the social media post doing such a thing like that could unconsciously provide a hero [image]. Like holding a gun, everyone bowing their head, they could have a different way of seeing it, ‘I’m more powerful than you guys. Before you were bullying me, before you were saying that I’m small, but now, holding this weapon gives me more power than all of you guys.’”

blocks.caption: [Be The Good] Not another school shooting please

blocks.text: This is what makes the Ateneo de Zamboanga school shooting particularly troubling. According to authorities, the shooter was a “very bright student” whom no one would have expected would do such a thing.
“It’s a wake-up call,” Cuevas said, “that even though someone is still performing, that doesn’t guarantee that your child is doing well emotionally.”

Sarte said this is why we need to be attentive and not so dismissive of early warning signs of mental health issues. Children aren’t just asking for attention or being dramatic — and being depressed or anxious isn’t something they want to happen to or that they set out to do.

And maybe that is what Filipino children need the most: families, schools, and communities that refrain from quick assumptions or dismissive attitudes, and instead are attentive, curious, and concerned about the heavy burdens their young hearts carry. – Rappler.com
Part 2 to be published on Saturday, August 29.
Elise Suarez is a Rappler intern from Puerto Princesa City and a Humanities student of the University of Asia & the Pacific.

articles.title: Inside the Philippines' shift from potential to progress in the ASEAN Battery race
articles.summary: Four editions into the ASEAN Battery Technology Conference, conversations around batteries, renewable energy, and electric mobility are becoming less about possibility and more about what it takes to…

blocks.text: Four editions into the ASEAN Battery Technology Conference, conversations around batteries, renewable energy, and electric mobility are becoming less about possibility and more about what it takes to make them work at scale.

The ASEAN Battery Technology Conference is one annual event I can hardly pass up, not simply because I have become invested in the subject, or because four years of covering batteries have convinced me that an electric vehicle might eventually be in my future. I keep coming back because of the progress I have been privileged to witness, understand, and, in some ways, embrace.

blocks.caption: Author Millie Manahan stands with Electric Vehicle Association of the Philippines Executive Director Jose Bienvenido Manuel Biona.

blocks.text: Author Millie Manahan stands with Electric Vehicle Association of the Philippines Executive Director Jose Bienvenido Manuel Biona.

When the conference first gathered industry leaders in Bali, Indonesia, in 2023, I remember asking myself and colleagues a straightforward question: Is the Philippines really ready for this, or are we simply one of the ASEAN countries participating in the conversation? Four editions later, I find myself asking a different one.

ABTC 2026 brought the regional battery community to Malaysia for three days of discussions. The opening day focused on ASEAN’s shift from research and innovation toward industrialization, manufacturing, safety, investment, and stronger regional collaboration.
The next two days brought that conversation closer to what all of this could mean on the ground, particularly for the Philippines.
Solar is growing. Storage needs to follow.
For Jose Rafael “Ping” Mendoza, president of the Philippine Solar and Storage Energy Alliance (PSSEA), the opportunity is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.

As more renewable energy, particularly solar, enters power grids, battery storage becomes critical. Solar produces electricity during the day, but batteries store that energy and deploy it when needed. Mendoza expects solar-plus-storage projects to become increasingly common across ASEAN, particularly at utility, commercial, and industrial scales.

In the Philippines, the sustainability argument becomes even more compelling outside major urban centres. Mendoza pointed to island and provincial communities where electricity still depends on diesel generation. These are areas where decentralised solar and battery systems could deliver significant economic and environmental benefits. But geography remains a challenge.
“In the Philippines, it’s cheaper to send something from Shanghai to Manila than Manila to somewhere else in the Philippines,” Mendoza said, A simple line that captured a complicated reality.
Deploying technology across more than 7,000 islands requires logistics, infrastructure, standards, regulation, and, ultimately, money.
When technology is ready, but capital is expensive
Cost of capital emerged as another recurring theme. Mendoza noted it as a barrier preventing existing technologies from reaching consumers at greater scale.
“The consumers are suffering, and there’s a lot of impact that the engineering solutions can provide, but the cost of capital is not going to wait,” he said.

This matters for sustainability. Solar panels, batteries, EVs, and charging infrastructure offer environmental benefits, but those benefits mean little if cleaner technology remains financially out of reach.
“The technology is maturing,” Mendoza said. “We need to capture this moment where everything’s going to change in the next five years, and we have to decide how we want to do it.”
That decision involves financing, incentives, infrastructure, regulation, and the role government chooses to play.
EV growth needs more than vehicles
Prof. Jose Bienvenido Manuel “Manny” Biona, executive director of the Electric Vehicle Association of the Philippines (EVAP), brought a similar reality to the EV discussion.
Biona identified three things the Philippines needs for EV investments to grow: consistent policy, investment-grade demand and a functioning EV ecosystem.

“There needs to be a consistent policy,” he said. Investments in manufacturing, charging networks and infrastructure are made over years, not political terms. Companies need confidence that today’s direction will continue beyond the current administration.

The recent approval of the Electric Vehicle Incentive Strategy (EVIS), signed under Executive Order No. 121 in July, is an important development. The program introduces performance-based fiscal support to encourage local EV and component manufacturing. But incentives are only one piece.

Manufacturers and investors also need confidence that Philippine demand will be strong and sustained. Then comes the ecosystem around that demand. It includes financing, charging, infrastructure readiness and ensuring all parts of the system develop at the same pace.
No single company controls all of these elements, which is why coordination and collaboration matter.
Four years later, a different conversation

Hioki E.E. Corporation has been part of ABTC’s journey since its beginnings, supporting the initiative as it grew into a platform connecting battery researchers, manufacturers, policymakers, investors and technology providers across ASEAN.

blocks.caption: Hioki E.E. Corp.,the Japanese electrical measurement technology company has supported the conference since its inaugural event in Bali, Indonesia, in 2023.

blocks.text: Hioki E.E. Corp.,the Japanese electrical measurement technology company has supported the conference since its inaugural event in Bali, Indonesia, in 2023.

Watching that community grow has made comparisons between countries inevitable. Malaysia has its strengths. Indonesia has resources and manufacturing ambitions. Singapore brings research, capital, and technology capabilities. Thailand has developed its EV and energy storage ecosystem. The Philippines has its own circumstances, opportunities, and challenges.

After four years of covering these conversations, I am less interested in asking who is ahead. The more useful question is whether each country is making meaningful progress with the strengths it already has.

Compared with the conversations I heard a year ago in Phuket, the Philippine discussion in Malaysia felt more concrete. We now have an approved EV incentive strategy. Solar and storage players are talking about scale, not merely potential. Industry is confronting financing, logistics, policy continuity and infrastructure rather than assuming technology alone will solve the transition.
There is still considerable work ahead. That is true not only for the Philippines, but across ASEAN.

But that question I first asked in Bali four years ago, about whether the Philippines was ready or merely participating? I may finally be getting my answer. And perhaps the clearest sign of it came at the very end of ABTC 2026.

blocks.caption: Jose Bienvenido Manuel Biona, executive director of the Electric Vehicle Association of the Philippines, accepts the ceremonial handover from Malaysian officials, designating the Philippines as the host of the 5th ASEAN Battery Technology Conference in 2027.

blocks.text: Jose Bienvenido Manuel Biona, executive director of the Electric Vehicle Association of the Philippines, accepts the ceremonial handover from Malaysian officials, designating the Philippines as the host of the 5th ASEAN Battery Technology Conference in 2027.
The handover brings the regional battery conversation to Philippine shores after previous editions in Bali, Singapore, Phuket, and Malaysia. That story deserves an article of its own.

articles.title: Malabon distributes over 3,000 laptops to public school teachers
articles.summary: More than 3,000 laptops were distributed by the Malabon city government to public school teachers to support their work and school-related duties. Mayor Jeannie Sandoval led the turnover ceremony at…

blocks.text: Malabon Mayor Jeannie Sandoval leads the distribution of laptops to public school educators during a ceremony at the Malabon Sports Complex on Thursday, Aug. 27. (Photo courtesy of the Malabon LGU)
More than 3,000 laptops were distributed by the Malabon city government to public school teachers to support their work and school-related duties.

blocks.caption: Malabon Mayor Jeannie Sandoval leads the distribution of laptops to public school educators during a ceremony at the Malabon Sports Complex on Thursday, Aug. 27. (Photo courtesy of the Malabon LGU)

blocks.text: Malabon Mayor Jeannie Sandoval leads the distribution of laptops to public school educators during a ceremony at the Malabon Sports Complex on Thursday, Aug. 27. (Photo courtesy of the Malabon LGU)

Mayor Jeannie Sandoval led the turnover ceremony at the Malabon Sports Complex on Thursday, Aug. 27, fulfilling her commitment to equip educators with essential tools to make their work more efficient and responsive to learners’ needs.
The laptops will help teachers prepare instructional materials, manage school tasks, access digital resources, and perform other responsibilities requiring technology.
Sandoval said the assistance would ease the workload of teachers and non-teaching personnel while improving the quality of services provided to students.

“This fulfills our promise to ensure that the work of our teachers and non-teaching personnel becomes easier and of better quality. You are the foundation of education and the good future of our students. Rest assured that the City Government will continue to support you,” Sandoval said.
Each qualified public school teacher also received a P4,500 second‑quarter allowance, giving added financial support in recognition of their dedication to Malabueño learners.

“The distribution of laptops and allowances is our way of recognizing the sacrifices and dedication of our teachers and non-teaching personnel. We want to ensure that they have enough support and equipment to properly perform their duties. When we support our teachers, our students and the entire community directly benefit,” City Administrator Alexander Rosete said.
The city government said the initiative strengthens its partnership with the education sector through programs and assistance that respond to the needs of educators and learners.

Also present during the turnover ceremony were Rep. Ricky Sandoval, Malabon Schools Division Superintendent Juan C. Obierna, CESO VI, officials of the Schools Division Office, and representatives of the Malabon Public Elementary and Secondary Teachers' Association Inc.

articles.title: ARTHACUP draws huge field at Sevina Park
articles.summary: Arthaland, the country’s foremost green developer, took its partnership with the Azkals Development Academy (ADA) to another level by staging ARTHACUP 2026 recently at the DLSU Laguna Football Field…

blocks.text: Arthaland, the country’s foremost green developer, took its partnership with the Azkals Development Academy (ADA) to another level by staging ARTHACUP 2026 recently at the DLSU Laguna Football Field beside Sevina Park in Biñan, Laguna.

The tournament brought together more than 1,100 young players, coaches, parents and guests as Arthaland bolstered its belief that building sustainable communities also means creating opportunities for the next generation.
It is also another way of putting this into practice, supporting young athletes as they develop their skills, confidence, and character through football.
The tournament drew players from ADA clubs and teams from Metro Manila, Southern Luzon and as far as Bacolod and Davao.
The tournament winners were Lingap Leads in the U-5 and U-13 categories, G8 Academy in U-7, LAOS FC in U-9 and Kaya FC in U-11.
“Sustainability goes beyond the environment. It is also about investing in people and
giving the next generation opportunities to grow,” said Pam Go, marketing and
corporate communications unit head of Arthaland.

“Football gives young players the chance to learn how to work as a team, handle challenges, and stay disciplined while enjoying the game. We appreciate Arthaland’s continued support of our young athletes,” said Stephen Schrock of the Azkals Development Academy.
Go added that ARTHACUP 2026 was a natural fit for Sevina Park, where an active and family-oriented lifestyle is part of everyday life.

For many participants, it was their first visit to Sevina Park, an 8.1-hectare community . planned by Sasaki Associates, which dedicated 60 percent of its land to green and open spaces. Its walkable, bicycle-friendly layout gives residents space to exercise, spend time outdoors, garden and gather with family and friends.

articles.title: Tate brothers blast US jail conditions as they seek bail in UK extradition fight
articles.summary: Andrew and Tristan Tate's legal team argued in a Miami court that the two were not a flight risk.

blocks.text: Andrew and Tristan Tate have told a Florida court they should be released from jail so they can fight extradition to the UK on charges of rape and trafficking.
Wearing tan jail uniforms, the brothers maintained they did not commit the alleged crimes as they slammed conditions in US custody.

Government lawyers argued that the two were a flight risk and had bragged about having multiple passports, while defence attorneys said the two social media influencers' high profile would make it almost impossible for them to flee.
US Magistrate Judge Lauren Louis will issue a written ruling at a later date on whether to grant bail to the dual British-US citizens. The two were arrested in Miami on 19 July.
During Thursday's hearing, defence lawyers said the pair had complied with the terms of their release while they battled the UK charges and another case in Romania.
US authorities took the men into custody last month after the UK's Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) unveiled dozens of new charges against them.
The British authorities have until 16 September to submit a full extradition request.
The brothers, who arrived in court in shackles, were questioned in turn by their defence attorneys and government lawyers as they took the stand.
Andrew Tate, 39, declared he has "never committed the crimes I'm accused of".
Tristan Tate, 38, described his detention conditions as small and hot, with little sunlight and exercise.
"It's beginning to grate on me because I can't partake in helping with my defence," he told the court, according to CBS News, the BBC's US partner.
"It's death by scurvy," he said, adding that he had lost 14lb (6.3kg).
The British Embassy filed court documents asking the judge to keep the Tates in custody as the UK pursues extradition.
US government lawyers pushed back against the brothers' claims that they had exaggerated their wealth to massage their online personas.
The federal attorneys said the Tates had access to resources that could help fund an escape and they had bragged about having multiple passports.
But Andrew Tate, a former professional kickboxer, testified that to support himself financially, he "had to go back to the boxing ring against heavier, younger opponents", according to CBS News.
"I've said some stupid things, but sometimes you have to shake the internet to get noticed," he testified about his online statements, according to CBS.
"This is the reality of the internet.
"I'm being treated like El Chapo," he added, referring to the Mexican drug kingpin, "but I have a perfect record in the court system".
Under questioning from his attorney, Joseph McBride, Andrew Tate denied he was a human trafficker.
The defence also called Natasha Sesay, from England, to testify in support of releasing Andrew Tate.
She described a five-year romantic relationship, saying she had had one child with him and was expecting a second.
"It's nice having him at home," she told the court, reports CBS.
Sesay also said that despite his online persona, Andrew Tate "has never ever been violent toward women", according to CBS.
The UK has brought a total of 59 criminal charges against the Tates, including rape and counts relating to sex trafficking and indecent images of a child.
The British authorities filed 21 charges last year against the brothers, then 38 additional counts last month.
The combined charges involve seven accusers, UK prosecutors said.
The brothers also faced sex-trafficking charges in Romania in 2022, and were under a travel ban until they were allowed to come to the US in 2025.
"If I go to England they will lock me up," Tristan Tate said on the stand in Miami on Thursday, "and take everything I've ever worked for".
He also said the Romanian charges had "destroyed my entire life", reports CBS.
"They took everything, even the savings accounts for their [his children's] college funds. This case is make or break for me."
The Tates built an influencer empire in the so-called manosphere, showcasing a lifestyle of conspicuous wealth and excess.
Andrew Tate accumulated millions of followers among an audience of primarily young men.
The White House has said President Donald Trump will not intervene in the extradition case of the brothers, who have been vocal supporters of him.

blocks.caption: Three out of four grizzlies in a family that was frequenting Nelson, B.C., have been killed. (The Ursa Project)

blocks.text: A third grizzly in a family of four well-known bears in the West Kootenay has been killed.
A sow and three yearlings attracted attention in the community of Nelson as they travelled throughout the community.
Wildlife officials said they had become a danger as they were habituated to humans and rummaged through yards and garbage.

The mother bear, which had previously been relocated from Nelson and returned, was killed earlier this month as was one of its yearlings, which the B.C. Conservation Officer Service said was not a suitable candidate for relocation due to its age and health. The young bear walked with a limp, either from injury or deformity.

items: More stories from the B.C. Interior
Grizzly bear family returns to Nelson, B.C., after attempted relocation

blocks.text: The two other yearlings, a male and female, were relocated but soon turned up again in the community of Christina Lake.
While the female has since moved on, officials say the male continued to frequent residential neighbourhoods and was deemed unsuitable for a second relocation attempt.
The service said Thursday that "the male yearling was dispatched, in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines."
Poor food sources
Provincial wildlife biologist Garth Mowat said the "bears were really habituated to people."

"We had lots of good indication that the bears had been eating human food for most years of their lives. We did this translocation as kind of a last effort and a hope that these bears would revert to wild food and we could save part of the family group."
Andrew Milne with the B.C. Conservation Officer Service said killing bears is only used as a last resort.

items: Young grizzly bear with limp killed in Nelson, B.C., sparks rally

blocks.text: "Killing wildlife in the name of public safety takes a toll on all these officers," he said. "We don't take these decisions lightly and we try to do as much as we can with what we have."

Mowat said with drought conditions throughout the B.C. Interior, berry crops are poor and more bears will be looking to come into communities in search of food. Officials are once again warning people to remove any possible attractants including fruit trees, garbage and bird feeders in order to prevent human-wildlife conflict.

articles.title: P1-billion fund revitalizes Project Noah. But they need more help reaching LGUs.
articles.summary: 'We can mainstream the science, the knowledge into the plans of the community,' says disaster risk management expert Mahar Lagmay

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Project Noah has been revitalized with a P1-billion fund release from the 2026 national budget, half of which will go to up-to-date equipment such as LiDAR drones and the rest to operations and its researchers.
Despite this newfound support to this long-running program, there remains the problem of reaching more local governments with knowledge and maps that scientists generate.

Project Noah is a hazard monitoring program launched in 2012, considered a landmark project in the Philippines’ disaster risk reduction and management. The Rodrigo Duterte administration pulled the plug on the program in 2017, which was then under the Department of Science and Technology. Project Noah did not completely disappear but with its termination, the program lost most of its experts and reach.
Currently, the University of the Philippines Resilience Institute (UPRI) manages Project Noah.

With the new funds, UPRI intends to prioritize using cutting-edge technology. This would allow it to generate higher resolution maps of major river basins, a huge improvement from the maps generated when Project Noah was launched 14 years ago. It will also continue promoting nature-based solutions to disaster risk reduction and management.

Mahar Lagmay, the institute’s executive director, listed down their priority areas in budget allocation such as: simulation of major detention basins, LiDAR drone surveys with educational institutions, native tree-mapping and inventory. Higher resolution is not just a quality issue; with it, UPRI researchers will be able to see where exactly flooding happens in a particular street.
Lagmay said they need help in disseminating information, including reaching more local governments so they can apply science to disaster risk management.

“We can mainstream the science, the knowledge into the plans of the community,” Lagmay said in a mix of Filipino and English on Thursday, August 27. “We want the plans of the community to be in accordance with the vision of the stakeholders.”
Lagmay said Project Noah will continue to prioritize support for the government’s flagship flood mitigation program Oplan Kontra Baha.

“The business of hazards mapping is not just to identify the hazards but more importantly to identify the safest places in the community for development and for citing evacuation centers,” Lagmay said.
According to Lagmay, UPRI has worked with at least 20 local governments on hazard and risk mapping in a span of eight years.
A notable partnership of UPRI was with the Quezon City local government. The result was a city-wide drainage master plan that relied on “science and nature-based solutions to mitigate flooding.”

All local governments UPRI has worked with “were really aggressive” and “wanted to change the system,” said Lagmay. Working with a local government to find ways to mitigate flooding and other hazards takes one to two years.
University of the Philippines President Angelo Jimenez said the university is “not an implementing arm” but only provides the knowledge and resource.
“It’s our mandate to offer this resource to the people,” Jimenez said in the same press briefing. “I believe that because of recent events, there is more appreciation of our work.”
He referred to the P1-billion funding as some sort of recognition, but it will need to be replenished if the government wants to continue Project NOAH. – Rappler.com
Quotes translated to English for brevity.
